definition_zh: 信仰；信心；信任；忠诚
definition_en: strong belief in a religion; firm trust in someone or something; a religion; loyalty and honesty in a relationship or promise
core_image: 在看不见终点时仍把手交给对方
scene: 我对她的判断有信心。I have faith in her judgement.
sceneCN: 这里 faith 是「信心、信任」（第 2 个义项）；句意：我对她的判断有信心。

senses.title: Religious belief
senses.definition: strong belief in a religion or in God
senses.definitionCN: 对宗教或上帝的坚定信仰
senses.example: Her faith gave her strength.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信仰给了她力量。
senses.why: The core sense is trust in what cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是对不可见之物的信任。

senses.title: Firm trust
senses.definition: firm trust in a person, plan, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、计划或想法的坚定信任
senses.example: We have faith in the new manager.
senses.exampleCN: 我们对新经理有信心。
senses.why: Religious trust extends to everyday confidence.
senses.whyCN: 宗教信任延伸到日常的信心。

senses.title: A religion
senses.definition: a particular religion or system of belief
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定宗教或信仰体系
senses.example: People of many faiths live here.
senses.exampleCN: 许多不同信仰的人住在这里。
senses.why: The belief becomes a named community.
senses.whyCN: 信仰变成有名号的群体。

senses.title: Loyalty
senses.definition: loyalty and honesty in a relationship or promise
senses.definitionCN: 在关系或承诺中的忠诚与诚实
senses.example: He kept faith with his old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老朋友信守情义。
senses.why: Trust between people becomes a bond of honour.
senses.whyCN: 人与人之间的信任成为信义纽带。

intro.en: Faith comes from Old French feid, from Latin fides, trust.
intro.cn: faith 来自古法语 feid，源头是拉丁语 fides（信任）。

items.en: Fides means trust or faithfulness.
items.cn: fides 意为信任或忠诚。

items.en: Fidere means to trust.
items.cn: fidere 意为信任。

items.en: Feid carries the sense of loyalty.
items.cn: feid 带有忠诚之义。

items.en: Faith means belief and promise.
items.cn: 中古英语中 faith 兼指信念与承诺。

items.en: Faith covers religion and personal trust.
items.cn: 现代英语中 faith 涵盖宗教与个人信任。

note.en: Faith is trust; fate is destiny.
note.cn: faith 是信任，fate 则是命运。

entries.definition: the feeling that something is true
a system of worship and belief

normalIntro.en: Faith is trust that holds even when proof is missing.
normalIntro.cn: faith 是在缺少证据时仍然坚持的信任。

normal.en: She never lost faith in her team.
normal.cn: 她从未对团队失去信心。

normal.en: They acted in good faith.
normal.cn: 他们出于善意行事。

normal.en: People of different faiths prayed together.
normal.cn: 不同信仰的人一起祈祷。

normal.en: He kept faith with his promise.
normal.cn: 他信守承诺。

normal.en: It was an act of faith to start the business.
normal.cn: 创办这家企业是一种信念之举。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching out in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中伸出的手。

abstract.en: Imagine a promise kept without witnesses.
abstract.cn: 想象没有见证人时仍守住的承诺。

abstract.en: Think of a light you trust before you see it.
abstract.cn: 把信仰想成一盏尚未看见却相信的灯。

examples.en: Her faith in people remained strong.
examples.cn: 她对人的信心依然坚定。

examples.en: The treaty was signed in good faith.
examples.cn: 条约是本着善意签署的。

examples.en: Patients need faith in their doctor.
examples.cn: 病人需要信任自己的医生。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: faith 与 fidelity、confide 同源于拉丁语 fides（信任），核心就是「信」。

root: faith 经由古法语 feid 来自拉丁语 fides（信任、忠诚），与 fidelity、confide 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Faith is religious belief, firm trust, a religion, or loyalty.
sensesIntro.cn: faith 指宗教信仰、坚定信任、某宗教，或忠诚信义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: trust offered without visible proof.
core.cn: 核心意象：在看不见证据时给予的信任。

branches.en: The base sense is trust in the unseen.
branches.cn: 基础义是对不可见之物的信任。

branches.en: Trust extends to people and plans.
branches.cn: 信任延伸到人与计划。

branches.en: The belief becomes a named religion.
branches.cn: 信仰变成有名号的宗教。

branches.en: Trust between people becomes loyalty.
branches.cn: 人与人之间的信任成为忠诚。

branches.en: Religious faith and personal honour both keep promises.
branches.cn: 宗教信仰与个人信义都守承诺。

intro.en: Faith builds faithful, faithfully, and faithless.
intro.cn: faith 构成 faithful、faithfully 与 faithless。

latinIntro.en: Latin fides and fidere explain faith and its Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fides 与 fidere 解释了 faith 及其拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 这座城市欢迎所有宗教。

items.example: He was faithless to his word.
The claim was made in bad faith.
We must keep faith with voters.

latinEntries.example: Fides is the root of faith.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fides 是 faith 的词根。
fidere 是 confide 的前身。

definition_zh: 假的；伪造的；赝品；冒牌货；冒充者；伪造；假装
definition_en: not genuine; a thing or a person that is not what it claims to be; to make a false copy or to pretend
core_image: 贴了真品标签的赝品花瓶，底款却是新刻的
scene: 拍卖行里，鉴定师拿起一只青花瓷瓶，看了一眼瓶底的款识就摇头。At the auction house, the expert glanced at the mark under the vase and called it fake.
sceneCN: 这里 fake 是「假的」（第 1 个义项：并非真品）；句意：拍卖行的鉴定师看了一眼瓶底的款识，就判定这只花瓶是假的。

collocations.zh: 假证件；伪造的身份证明

derivatives.zh: 冒充者；骗子（fake 加 -er 构成施动者名词）
造假行为；赝品（fake 加 -ery 构成行为或产物名词）
伪造的；假造的（fake 加 -ed 构成的形容词）

senses.title: Not genuine
senses.definition: made to look real or valuable in order to deceive people
senses.definitionCN: 做得像真的或很有价值，目的是骗人
senses.example: The expert said the signature was fake.
senses.exampleCN: 专家说那个签名是假的。
senses.why: Fake began in thieves slang as a word for a thing made to deceive, so the adjective that labels the false object is the oldest everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: fake 最早是盗贼俚语里指「为骗人而做的东西」，所以给假物件定性的形容词是最早的日常义项。

senses.title: A counterfeit object
senses.definition: an object, especially a work of art, that has been copied and passed off as genuine
senses.definitionCN: 复制后冒充真品的物件，尤指艺术品
senses.example: The gallery pulled three fakes from the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊从拍卖中撤下了三件赝品。
senses.why: Once the adjective could stand before a noun, it could also stand alone as a noun naming the counterfeit itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词既然能放在名词前，也就能独立成名词，直接指赝品本身。

senses.title: A person who pretends
senses.definition: someone who adopts a false identity or a false manner in order to deceive others
senses.definitionCN: 用假身份或假做派欺骗他人的人
senses.example: He turned out to be a fake who had never worked there.
senses.exampleCN: 原来他是个从未在那里工作过的冒充者。
senses.why: A person can be a copy of a person, so the noun extends from false objects to false identities.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是「人的仿制品」，于是名词从假物件扩展到假身份。

senses.title: To counterfeit
senses.definition: to make a copy of something valuable in order to deceive people
senses.definitionCN: 复制贵重物品以欺骗他人
senses.example: The gang faked passports for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 那伙人为越境伪造了护照。
senses.why: The verb names the act behind the adjective: making a thing that is not what it seems.
senses.whyCN: 动词命名的正是形容词背后的动作：做出「看着不像它本身」的东西。

senses.title: To pretend
senses.definition: to pretend to feel something or to be something, often in order to avoid trouble
senses.definitionCN: 假装有某种感受或某种身份，常为逃避麻烦
senses.example: She faked a headache to leave the meeting early.
senses.exampleCN: 她假装头疼，提前离开了会议。
senses.why: Pretending a feeling is counterfeiting something inner, so the forging verb moves from objects to emotions.
senses.whyCN: 假装一种感受，是伪造内心之物，于是「伪造」这个动词从物件移到情感。

senses.title: Insincere, put on
senses.definition: not sincere, produced only for show
senses.definitionCN: 不真诚的，只为做样子而表现的
senses.example: His fake cheerfulness convinced nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 他那做作的欢快骗不了任何人。
senses.why: The adjective turns back on behaviour: a show that is performed rather than felt is itself a fake.
senses.whyCN: 形容词又反过来修饰行为：演出来而非真有的表现，本身就是假的。

intro.en: Fake is generally traced to late eighteenth century English thieves slang, and no secure earlier source has been found; it is not a Latin word, though the feign family is its nearest Latin relative in meaning.
intro.cn: fake 一般认为出自十八世纪末的英国盗贼俚语，更早的来源没有可靠结论；它不是拉丁语词，但在意义上最近的一系是拉丁语 fingere 所生的 feign 家族。

items.en: Fake is first recorded in English thieves slang, and its deeper source is unknown.
items.cn: fake 最早见于英国盗贼俚语，更深来源不确定。

items.en: The slang verb is recorded in the sense of doing for or robbing a person, and its link to counterfeiting is probable rather than certain.
items.cn: 这一俚语动词有「替人做掉、抢劫」的用法，它与「造假」之间的联系只是较大可能，而非确证。

items.en: Fake becomes a noun and an adjective for counterfeit goods, banknotes, and works of art.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，fake 作名词和形容词，指假货、假钞与假艺术品。

items.en: The verb widens from forging objects to pretending feelings and illnesses.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，动词从伪造物件扩展到假装情感与疾病。

items.en: Fake news, fake IDs, and digital fakes keep the word productive in new media.
items.cn: 假新闻、假证件与数字造假让这个词在新媒体中继续孳生。

note.en: Fake sits beside its own English family and beside the Latin feign group, which shares the meaning but not the origin.
note.cn: fake 旁边既有英语自身的词族，也有意义相近、来源不同的拉丁 feign 一系。

entries.definitionCN: 冒充者；骗子（由 fake 加 -er 构成）

entries.definition: the making of fakes, or a fake thing
entries.definitionCN: 造假；赝品（由 fake 加 -ery 构成）
假装；佯装。与 fake 音义相近，但词源不同：feign 来自拉丁语 fingere（塑造）

entries.definition: a copy made to deceive people
a forged document or work of art

normalIntro.en: Fake is a short word that lives in fixed phrases: fake news, fake IDs, fake smiles, and the verb phrase to fake it.
normalIntro.cn: fake 是个短词，常出现在固定说法里：「fake news」「fake ID」「fake smile」，以及动词短语「fake it」。

normal.en: Fake news is false reporting spread as if it were real news.
normal.cn: 假新闻是以真新闻的样子传播的虚假报道。

normal.en: A fake ID is a forged document that proves a false identity.
normal.cn: 假证件是证明虚假身份的伪造文件。

normal.en: To fake it is to pretend that you can do something.
normal.cn: fake it 就是装作自己会做某事。

normal.en: A faker is a person who fakes, and fakery is the practice.
normal.cn: faker 是造假的人，fakery 是造假这种行为。

normal.en: A fake smile shows a feeling that is not there.
normal.cn: 假笑展示的是一种并不存在的感受。

abstract.en: Picture a vase with a fresh mark cut into old clay.
abstract.cn: 想象一只花瓶，旧胎上新刻了款识。

abstract.en: Picture a museum shelf holding a copy where the original should be.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆的架上，真品的位置摆着一件复制品。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger wearing a name badge that is not his.
abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人戴着不属于自己的名牌。

examples.en: The dealer sold him a fake watch for a huge sum.
examples.cn: 商人把一只假表以高价卖给了他。

examples.en: She faked an injury to avoid the final run.
examples.cn: 她假装受伤，以逃避最后一轮跑步。

examples.en: The report called the document fake and refused to publish it.
examples.cn: 报告称该文件是伪造的，拒绝刊发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费克」——花大钱买了个漂亮的壳，看着像真的，其实是假货；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为 fake 出自十八世纪末的英国盗贼俚语，指「做手脚、造假」，更深词源不确定；它不是拉丁语词，意义上的近亲是拉丁语 fingere（塑造、捏造）所生的 feign 一系。

sensesIntro.en: Fake starts as a label for a false object, splits into the counterfeit thing and the impostor, turns into the act of forging, and ends with pretended feeling and insincere show.
sensesIntro.cn: fake 先给假物件定性，再分成赝品与冒充者，随后转为伪造的动作，最后落在假装的情感与做作的表现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vase that carries a genuine label but a newly cut mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴着真品标签、底款却是新刻的花瓶。

branches.en: The adjective for a false object is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 给假物件定性的形容词是日常义项。

branches.en: The noun for the counterfeit object stands alone.
branches.cn: 指赝品的名词可以独立使用。

branches.en: A false person is a counterfeit of a human being.
branches.cn: 假人是「人的仿制品」。

branches.en: The verb names the act of making the false copy.
branches.cn: 动词指做出假复制品的动作。

branches.en: Pretended feeling and performed behaviour are counterfeits of the inner life.
branches.cn: 假装的情感与演出来的表现，都是内心生活的赝品。

intro.en: Fake has no confirmed Latin root; its family is English, while the nearest Latin relative in meaning is the feign group built on fingere, to shape or mould.
intro.cn: fake 没有确证的拉丁词根，词族是英语自身；意义上最接近的拉丁一系，是拉丁语 fingere（塑造）所生的 feign 家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fingere means to shape, mould, or invent; its participle fictus and noun fictio give English feign, fiction, and fictitious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fingere 意为塑造、捏造；其分词 fictus 与名词 fictio 带来英语的 feign、fiction 与 fictitious。

items.example: Fake is the short English word at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: fake 是这一族的英语核心词。

items.meaning: action or product of an act

items.example: Feign comes from Latin fingere and means to pretend.
items.exampleCN: feign 来自拉丁语 fingere，意为假装。

items.example: Fingere is the source of the feign family.
items.exampleCN: fingere 是 feign 一系的源头。

items.example: Fictus is the participle behind fiction.
items.exampleCN: fictus 是 fiction 背后的分词。
fictitious 描述被编造出来的东西。

items.example: Figment is a thing shaped by the mind.
items.exampleCN: figment 是头脑塑造出来的东西。

definition_zh: 隼；猎隼；雌隼；隼一般迅捷的人；隼形徽记
definition_en: a fast bird of prey with long pointed wings; also the female of the species, a trained hunting bird, or a symbol of speed
core_image: 一只收拢双翼的隼，从高空笔直俯冲，爪尖像镰刀
scene: 清晨的草原上，一只猛禽收拢双翼，笔直地俯冲下来。At dawn on the grassland, a falcon folded its wings and dived straight at its prey.
sceneCN: 这里 falcon 是「隼」（第 1 个义项：一种猛禽）；句意：黎明时，一只隼收拢双翼，笔直俯冲扑向猎物。

derivatives.zh: 养隼者；猎鹰人（falcon 加 -er 构成施动者名词）
猎鹰术；放鹰捕猎（falcon 加 -ry 构成行业名词）
隼的；似隼的（falcon 加 -ine 构成形容词）

senses.title: A bird of prey
senses.definition: a fast bird of prey with long pointed wings, a hooked beak, and sharp talons
senses.definitionCN: 一种猛禽，双翼长而尖，喙钩曲，爪锋利
senses.example: A falcon can hover almost still in a strong wind.
senses.exampleCN: 隼能在强风中几乎静止地悬停。
senses.why: The bird is named for its hooked, sickle-shaped profile, so the first sense is simply the living raptor.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟因钩曲的镰刀形轮廓得名，所以第一个义项就是这种活生生的猛禽。

senses.title: The female bird
senses.definition: in falconry, the female of the species, which is larger and preferred for hunting
senses.definitionCN: 在猎鹰术中指该物种的雌鸟，体型更大，更常用于狩猎
senses.example: In falconry the female bird alone is called a falcon.
senses.exampleCN: 在猎鹰术中，只有雌鸟才被称为 falcon。
senses.why: Falconry gave the word a precise technical sense: the female, larger and preferred for hunting, is the falcon proper.
senses.whyCN: 猎鹰术赋予这个词精确的技术含义：体型更大、更受青睐的雌鸟才是严格意义上的 falcon。

senses.title: A trained hunting bird
senses.definition: a falcon that has been trained to hunt for a person
senses.definitionCN: 经过训练、替人捕猎的隼
senses.example: The keeper released the falcon at the edge of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养者在树林边放飞了猎隼。
senses.why: A bird that is trained stops being only a species and becomes a working partner, which is the hunting sense.
senses.whyCN: 经过训练的鸟不再只是一个物种，而成为干活的伙伴，这就是狩猎义项。

senses.title: A swift, fierce figure
senses.definition: a person who moves or strikes with the speed and fierceness of a falcon
senses.definitionCN: 行动或出击像隼一样迅速凶猛的人
senses.example: She fell on the loose ball like a falcon on a hare.
senses.exampleCN: 她像隼扑野兔一样扑向那个松脱的球。
senses.why: Speed and a straight dive invite the metaphor of a person who strikes fast and without mercy.
senses.whyCN: 速度和笔直的俯冲让人想到出手快而毫不留情的人，隐喻由此而来。

senses.title: An emblem of speed
senses.definition: a picture or figure of a falcon used as a symbol on a badge, coin, or flag
senses.definitionCN: 用于徽章、钱币或旗帜上的隼的形象，作为象征
senses.example: The old coin bears a falcon with spread wings.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚古币上铸着一只展翅的隼。
senses.why: An emblem borrows the shape of the bird to stand for speed or watchfulness, detached from the animal itself.
senses.whyCN: 徽记借鸟的形状来象征速度或警觉，已经与动物本身分离。

intro.en: Falcon reached English through Old French, and the bird name is generally traced to Latin falx, a sickle, for the hooked shape of its wings or talons; a Germanic source has also been suggested, so the origin is not fully settled.
intro.cn: falcon 经古法语进入英语；鸟名一般认为出自拉丁语 falx（镰刀），得名于镰刀形的翅膀或钩爪；也有人提出日耳曼语来源，所以词源并无定论。

items.en: Falx, genitive falcis, means a sickle or a curved blade, and its stem falc- supplies the shape.
items.cn: falx（属格 falcis）意为镰刀或弯刀，词干 falc- 提供「弯钩形」这一意象。

items.en: Falco, falconem is recorded as the name of the bird, probably from the sickle shape of its wings or claws.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 falco（宾格 falconem）已用作这种鸟的名称，一般认为得名于镰刀形的翅膀或钩爪。

items.en: Faucon carries the bird name into Old French.
items.cn: faucon 把这一鸟名带进古法语。

items.en: English takes faucon and settles on the spelling falcon.
items.cn: 英语吸收 faucon，并逐渐固定为 falcon 的拼写。

items.en: Falconry, falconer, and falconine extend the bird word into sport and description.
items.cn: falconry、falconer 与 falconine 把这一鸟名扩展到狩猎活动与描写用语。

note.en: Falcon keeps a small English family of its own, and its meaning sits inside the wider field of birds of prey.
note.cn: falcon 有自己的一小族英语派生词，意义上则落在「猛禽」这个更大的义场里。

entries.definition: a person who keeps and trains falcons
entries.definitionCN: 养隼者；猎鹰人（由 falcon 加 -er 构成）

entries.definition: the sport of training falcons to hunt
entries.definitionCN: 猎鹰术；放鹰捕猎（由 falcon 加 -ry 构成）

entries.definition: relating to or resembling a falcon
entries.definitionCN: 隼的；似隼的（由 falcon 加 -ine 构成）

entries.definition: a bird of prey with broad wings and a long tail
a very large and powerful bird of prey
any bird of prey, such as a hawk, falcon, or owl

normalIntro.en: Falcon is a bird word first, and most of its family comes from falconry: a falconer flies a falcon, and falconry is the sport.
normalIntro.cn: falcon 首先是个鸟名，它的大部分词族都来自猎鹰活动：falconer 放飞 falcon，falconry 是这项运动。

normal.en: A falcon is a bird of prey with long pointed wings.
normal.cn: 隼是一种双翼长而尖的猛禽。

normal.en: A falconer is the person who keeps and flies a falcon.
normal.cn: falconer 是饲养并放飞隼的人。

normal.en: Falconry is the sport of training falcons to hunt.
normal.cn: falconry 是训练隼来捕猎的运动。

normal.en: The peregrine falcon is famous for its steep dive.
normal.cn: 游隼以陡直的俯冲闻名。

normal.en: Falconine means hawk-like and keeps the same root.
normal.cn: falconine 意为似隼的，保留同一个词根。

abstract.en: Picture a sickle curve drawn along the edge of a wing.
abstract.cn: 想象沿着翅膀边缘画出一道镰刀般的弧线。

abstract.en: Picture a hooded female bird sitting still on a fist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只戴着头罩的雌隼，稳稳地停在拳头上。

abstract.en: Picture the hood lifted and the bird launched at a hare.
abstract.cn: 想象头罩被揭开，隼朝野兔冲了出去。

examples.en: A falcon hovered above the ridge, watching the meadow.
examples.cn: 一只隼悬停在山脊上方，注视着草地。

examples.en: The falconer carried his falcon to the field at dawn.
examples.cn: 猎鹰人在黎明时把隼带到田野。

examples.en: The team chose a falcon as its emblem.
examples.cn: 这支队伍选了一只隼作为徽记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法尔肯」——法尔肯像一支射出去的箭，又快又准，说的其实是隼；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 falx（属格 falcis，镰刀）→ 晚期拉丁语 falco（隼，一般认为得名于镰刀形的翅膀或钩爪）→ 古法语 faucon → 英语 falcon；也有人主张日耳曼语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Falcon moves from the living bird to the female bird of falconry, to the trained hunter, and then to metaphorical speed and to an emblem.
sensesIntro.cn: falcon 从活生生的鸟，走到猎鹰术里的雌鸟，再到受训的猎手，最后引申为迅捷的隐喻与徽记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sickle-shaped wing folded for a straight dive.
core.cn: 核心意象：镰刀形的翅膀收拢，准备笔直俯冲。

branches.en: The living raptor is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 活生生的猛禽是日常义项。

branches.en: The female bird is the technical falconry sense.
branches.cn: 雌鸟是猎鹰术里的技术义项。

branches.en: The trained bird is the working hunter.
branches.cn: 受训的鸟是干活儿的猎手。

branches.en: A fast, fierce person borrows the dive.
branches.cn: 迅捷凶猛的人借用了俯冲的意象。

branches.en: An emblem keeps only the shape and the idea of speed.
branches.cn: 徽记只保留形状与速度的概念。

intro.en: Falcon rests on the Latin noun falx, falcis, a sickle, whose stem falc- describes the hooked shape of the bird; English adds falconer, falconry, and falconine around it.
intro.cn: falcon 的拉丁源头是名词 falx（属格 falcis，镰刀），词干 falc- 描摹隼的镰刀形弯钩；英语围绕它加上 -er、-ry、-ine 构成同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin falx means sickle, and its stem falc- appears in falcon and in Latin words for hooked or curved things.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 falx 意为镰刀，其词干 falc- 出现在 falcon，也出现在拉丁语中表示弯钩之物的词里。

items.example: Falx is the shape behind the name.
items.exampleCN: falx 是名字背后的形状。

items.example: The stem falc- joins Latin compounds.
items.exampleCN: 词干 falc- 参与构成拉丁语复合词。
falcon 承载着镰刀的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ine turns nouns into adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ine 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Falcate keeps the pure shape meaning.
items.exampleCN: falcate 保留纯粹的「镰刀形」含义。
falciform 把 falc- 与 form 组合起来。

items.meaning: a cutting away, especially of funds
items.example: Defalcation uses the same cutting image.
items.exampleCN: defalcation 沿用同一个「切割」意象。

definition_zh: 落下；下降；跌倒；进入某种状态；秋天
definition_en: to move downward under gravity; to decrease in amount or level; to lose balance and go down; to pass into a state; the season of autumn
core_image: 一片叶子离开枝头，旋转着落向地面
scene: 秋天树叶纷纷落下。Leaves fall from the trees in autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 fall 是「落下」（第 1 个义项）；句意：秋天树叶纷纷落下。

senses.title: To move downward
senses.definition: to move downward under the force of gravity
senses.definitionCN: 在重力作用下向下移动
senses.example: The leaves fall in October.
senses.exampleCN: 树叶在十月落下。
senses.why: The core sense is the pull of gravity.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是重力的拉扯。

senses.title: To decrease
senses.definition: to decrease in amount, level, or value
senses.definitionCN: 数量、水平或价值下降
senses.example: Prices fell sharply last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月价格大幅下跌。
senses.why: A falling number moves down like a falling object.
senses.whyCN: 下降的数字像下落的物体一样走低。

senses.title: To lose balance
senses.definition: to lose balance and go down to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 失去平衡倒向地面
senses.example: He fell on the icy path.
senses.exampleCN: 他在结冰的小路上摔倒了。
senses.why: The body drops when it can no longer stand.
senses.whyCN: 身体无法站稳时就会倒下。

senses.title: To pass into a state
senses.definition: to pass suddenly into a particular state or condition
senses.definitionCN: 突然进入某种状态或状况
senses.example: The baby fell asleep in her arms.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在她怀里睡着了。
senses.why: Falling into a state is like dropping into it.
senses.whyCN: 「落入」某种状态就像掉进去。

senses.title: Autumn
senses.definition: the season between summer and winter, especially in American English; also an act of falling
senses.definitionCN: 夏冬之间的季节，尤用于美式英语；也指下落的行为
senses.example: The leaves turn gold in the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天树叶变成金黄色。
senses.why: The season is named for the falling of leaves.
senses.whyCN: 这个季节因落叶而得名。

intro.en: Fall comes from Old English feallan; the autumn sense comes from the fall of the leaf.
intro.cn: fall 源自古英语 feallan；秋天义来自「落叶时节」的说法。

items.en: A common root means to fall.
items.cn: 共同的词根意为落下。

items.en: Feallan means to drop down.
items.cn: feallan 意为落下。

items.en: Fall develops figurative senses.
items.cn: 中古英语中 fall 发展出比喻义。

items.en: The fall of the leaf names autumn.
items.cn: the fall of the leaf 用来指秋天。

items.en: Fall becomes the usual word for autumn.
items.cn: 美式英语中 fall 成为秋天的常用词。

note.en: Fall means to drop; fail means to not succeed.
note.cn: fall 是落下，fail 则是失败。

normalIntro.en: Fall covers gravity, numbers, bodies, states, and the autumn season.
normalIntro.cn: fall 涵盖重力、数字、身体、状态与秋季。

normal.en: Rain fell all night.
normal.cn: 雨下了一整夜。

normal.en: The temperature fell below zero.
normal.cn: 气温降到了零下。

normal.en: She fell down the stairs.
normal.cn: 她从楼梯上摔了下来。

normal.en: He fell asleep during the film.
normal.cn: 他看电影时睡着了。

normal.en: We visit the farm every fall.
normal.cn: 我们每年秋天都去农场。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf letting go of its branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子松开树枝。

abstract.en: Imagine a number sliding down a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象数字沿图表下滑。

abstract.en: Think of a body folding gently to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象身体轻轻倒向地面。

examples.en: Snow began to fall at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时开始下雪。

examples.en: Sales fell by ten percent.
examples.cn: 销售额下降了百分之十。

examples.en: The old tree fell in the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨中那棵老树倒了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fall 是英语本族词；美式英语用 the fall 表示「秋天」，因为这是树叶飘落的季节。

root: fall 源自古英语 feallan（落下），属日耳曼语族；秋天义来自 the fall of the leaf（落叶时节）。

sensesIntro.en: Fall means to drop, decrease, tumble, enter a state, or the season of autumn.
sensesIntro.cn: fall 意为落下、下降、跌倒、进入某状态，或秋天。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf letting go and drifting down.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶子松开枝头飘落。

branches.en: The base sense is downward movement.
branches.cn: 基础义是向下移动。

branches.en: Numbers and values move down too.
branches.cn: 数字与价值也会走低。

branches.en: A body that loses balance falls.
branches.cn: 失去平衡的身体会倒下。

branches.en: States are entered as if by falling into them.
branches.cn: 状态像是掉进去一样被进入。

branches.en: The season is named for falling leaves.
branches.cn: 这个季节因落叶得名。

intro.en: Fall forms compounds such as waterfall and phrasal verbs such as fall down.
intro.cn: fall 构成 waterfall 等复合词与 fall down 等短语动词。

latinIntro.en: Fall is a Germanic word with no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: fall 是日耳曼词，没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to drop or the act of dropping
items.example: The cup fell from the table.
The apple fell to the ground.
The fallen leaves covered the path.
The waterfall is fifty metres high.

items.exampleCN: 这场争端造成了严重后果。
我们需要一个备用方案。

definition_zh: 可能出错的；易犯错的；不可靠的
definition_en: capable of making mistakes or being wrong
core_image: 一把尺子的边缘有一道几乎看不见的弯，用久了才在长线上显出偏差
scene: 他在报告末尾写下一行小字，承认自己的估算可能偏差。The most careful method is still fallible at the edges.
sceneCN: 这里 fallible 指可能出错的（第 4 个义项：会出错的方法或系统）；句意为最细致的方法在边缘处仍会出错。

pos.zh: 可能出错的；易犯错的；不可靠的

senses.title: Capable of error
senses.definition: able to be mistaken, as every person is
senses.definitionCN: 可能判断错误，凡是人皆如此
senses.example: Any fallible reader can misread a single line.
senses.exampleCN: 任何会犯错的读者都可能看错一行。
senses.why: The word is not an insult; it states a condition shared by all thinking beings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不是侮辱；它陈述一切思考者共有的条件。

senses.title: Fallible memory
senses.definition: a memory that changes or invents detail over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间改变或增添细节的记忆
senses.example: Her fallible memory turned three events into one.
senses.exampleCN: 她不可靠的记忆把三件事合为一件。
senses.why: Memory is not a recording but a reconstruction, and reconstruction can drift.
senses.whyCN: 记忆不是录音，而是重建，而重建会漂移。

senses.title: Fallible judgement
senses.definition: a decision that may be reasonable yet still wrong
senses.definitionCN: 可能合理却仍然错误的决定
senses.example: Even fallible judgement deserves to be heard.
senses.exampleCN: 即使可能出错的判断也值得被听见。
senses.why: A judgement that might be wrong still carries information that silence cannot.
senses.whyCN: 可能出错的判断仍携带沉默无法提供的信息。

senses.title: Fallible system
senses.definition: a method or machine that can fail at its limits
senses.definitionCN: 在极限处可能失效的方法或机器
senses.example: The most careful method is still fallible at the edges.
senses.exampleCN: 最细致的方法在边缘处仍会出错。
senses.why: A system is fallible not because it is badly built but because the world exceeds its rules.
senses.whyCN: 系统的易错不在于造得差，而在于世界超出了它的规则。

senses.title: Fallible authority
senses.definition: an expert or office whose word is not automatically true
senses.definitionCN: 其话并非自动为真的专家或机构
senses.example: Fallible authority still beats no authority at all.
senses.exampleCN: 会错的权威仍胜于完全没有权威。
senses.why: The word separates respect from surrender: an authority may be trusted without being treated as a god.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把尊重与投降分开：权威可以被信任，却不必被当作神。

senses.title: Human fallibility
senses.definition: the general condition that people can always be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 人总可能出错的普遍状况
senses.example: The design assumes human fallibility and adds a second check.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计预设人会出错，于是加了第二道检查。
senses.why: Good design does not deny the weakness; it plans for it.
senses.whyCN: 好的设计不否认弱点，而是为它作准备。

senses.title: Fallible proof
senses.definition: evidence that is strong but not beyond every doubt
senses.definitionCN: 有力却未超越一切怀疑的证据
senses.example: The case rested on fallible proof and a careful jury.
senses.exampleCN: 案子依靠不完美的证据与谨慎的陪审团。
senses.why: Most real proofs are strong without being airtight, and decisions must still be made.
senses.whyCN: 现实中的多数证明有力却不严密，而决定仍必须作出。

senses.title: Fallible but honest
senses.definition: a person who errs without intending to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 会出错却无意欺骗的人
senses.example: He was fallible but honest, and that was enough.
senses.exampleCN: 他会犯错，但诚实，这就够了。
senses.why: The word does not imply deceit; it only denies perfection.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不含欺骗之意；它只是否认完美。

intro.en: Fallible comes from a Latin verb meaning to deceive, so it names the capacity to be led astray.
intro.cn: fallible 来自一个意为「欺骗」的拉丁动词，因此它命名的是被引离正道的能力。

items.en: English took the adjective in the 17c., often in theology and law.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，常见于神学与法律。

items.en: Fallere meant 'to deceive, to trip up', the root of false and fail.
items.cn: fallere 意为「欺骗、使失足」，是 false 与 fail 的词根。

items.en: Fallibilis meant 'that can deceive or be deceived'.
items.cn: fallibilis 意为「能欺骗或能被欺骗的」。

items.en: Science adopted the word to state that all findings can be revised.
items.cn: 科学采用这个词，用来声明一切结论都可被修正。

items.en: Everyday English softened it: fallible now mostly means human, not deceitful.
items.cn: 日常英语把它软化：如今 fallible 多指「有人性的」，而非「欺骗的」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the false root; the near-meaning group names kinds of unreliability.
note.cn: 形近组共享「假」的词根；近义组列出不可靠的不同种类。

entries.definition: the state of being unable to err.
cannot be trusted to work or tell truth.

entries.definitionCN: 基于错误、事实上不对的。

entries.definition: holding a wrong idea about something.

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a ruler with a bend so slight that only a long line reveals it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一把尺子有一道极轻的弯，只有长线才显出它」的画面。

normal.en: Fallible shares a root with false and fail: all three are about coming off the true line.
normal.cn: fallible 与 false、fail 同根：三者都与偏离真线有关。

normal.en: Add in- and the word flips: infallible means cannot fall.
normal.cn: 加上 in- 词就翻转：infallible 意为「不会失足」。

normal.en: Think of a witness who is honest and still wrong.
normal.cn: 想象一个诚实却仍然记错的证人。

normal.en: Say FAL-uh-bl; the first syllable is the stumble itself.
normal.cn: 读成 FAL-uh-bl，第一个音节就是那一下踉跄。

normal.en: Link with default: both suggest a small built-in chance of failure.
normal.cn: 和 default 联系：两者都暗示内置的一点失败可能。

abstract.en: Admitting fallibility is the beginning of every reliable method.
abstract.cn: 承认易错，是一切可靠方法的开始。

abstract.en: The opposite of fallible is not wise; it is impossible.
abstract.cn: 易错的反面不是智慧，而是不可能。

abstract.en: Being wrong is not the same as being false; honest error still deserves respect.
abstract.cn: 出错不等于虚假；诚实的错误仍值得尊重。

examples.en: Any fallible reader can misread a single line.
examples.cn: 任何会犯错的读者都可能看错一行。

examples.en: The most careful method is still fallible at the edges.
examples.cn: 最细致的方法在边缘处仍会出错。

examples.en: He was fallible but honest, and that was enough.
examples.cn: 他会犯错，但诚实，这就够了。

dict_mnemonic.text: fall（跌、骗）+ ible（能……的）：能被绊倒的，就是「会出错的」。

root: 拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、使失足）→ fallibilis（可能被欺的）

sensesIntro.en: Fallible never means dishonest; it means able to come off the true line, and the senses differ in what may slip.
sensesIntro.cn: fallible 从不指不诚实；它指可能偏离真线，各义项的差别在于滑开的是什么。

core.en: ABLE TO COME OFF THE TRUE LINE
core.cn: 可能偏离真线

branches.en: The general human condition, without any hint of deceit.
branches.cn: 普遍的人类处境，不含欺骗之意。

branches.en: Memory and judgement that drift.
branches.cn: 会漂移的记忆与判断。

branches.en: Systems and proofs that fail at their limits.
branches.cn: 在极限处失效的系统与证明。

branches.en: Authorities that are respected but not worshipped.
branches.cn: 受尊重却不被崇拜的权威。

branches.en: Design that plans for the weakness instead of denying it.
branches.cn: 为弱点作准备而非否认它的设计。

intro.en: The fall family is about slipping: fallible can slip, infallible cannot, and fallacy is the slip itself.
intro.cn: fall 词族与滑倒有关：fallible 会滑，infallible 不会，fallacy 则是那一下滑。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere means to deceive or trip; its family includes false, fail and fault, all forms of coming off the line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 意为欺骗或绊倒；其词族包括 false、fail 与 fault，都是偏离真线的形态。

items.exampleCN: 会犯错的法官仍在裁判。

items.example: Fallibility is part of the method.
items.exampleCN: 易错性是方法的一部分。

items.example: The argument rests on a fallacy.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证基于一个谬误。

items.example: The plan failed on day two.
The fault was in the seal.

definition_zh: 休耕的；休耕地；闲置的；停滞的；淡黄褐色的
definition_en: left unsown so that the soil can recover; land in that state; inactive or unused; pale yellowish-brown
core_image: 一块空了一季的田，只有短草和泥土在晒太阳
scene: 秋收之后，这片田地空着不种，让泥土休息一季。After the harvest, the field lay fallow for a season to let the soil rest.
sceneCN: 这里 fallow 是「休耕的」（第 1 个义项：田地暂时不种作物）；句意：秋收之后，这块田休耕一季，让土壤恢复。

pos.zh: 休耕的；闲置的；淡黄褐色的

derivatives.zh: 休耕状态；闲置状态（fallow 加 -ness 构成抽象名词）
休耕；让土地休闲（fallow 加 -ing 构成动名词）

senses.title: Land left unsown
senses.definition: describes land that is ploughed but left without a crop for a season so that it can recover
senses.definitionCN: 指翻耕后一季不种作物、以便恢复地力的田地
senses.example: The farmer left the wet field fallow for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫让那块湿田休耕了一年。
senses.why: Old English fealh named land ploughed and left unsown, so the first sense is the field at rest.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fealh 指翻耕后闲置不种的土地，所以第一个义项就是「歇着的田」。

senses.title: Such land as a noun
senses.definition: a piece of land that is left unsown for a season
senses.definitionCN: 一季不种作物的那块土地
senses.example: A narrow fallow divided the wheat from the barley.
senses.exampleCN: 一条窄窄的休耕地把小麦和大麦分开。
senses.why: The adjective could stand alone, and the noun fixed the piece of land itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可以独立使用，名词便固定指那块土地本身。

senses.title: A dormant period
senses.definition: describes a period of time when activity is deliberately stopped
senses.definitionCN: 指活动被有意暂停的一段时间
senses.example: The studio went through a fallow period after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾之后，这间工作室经历了一段停滞期。
senses.why: A field that rests for a season becomes the model for any period of deliberate inactivity.
senses.whyCN: 一季休整的田，成了任何有意停顿的时期的模型。

senses.title: Pale yellowish-brown
senses.definition: describes a pale brownish-yellow colour, especially of an animal coat
senses.definitionCN: 指淡黄褐色，尤指动物毛色
senses.example: The fallow coat of the deer blended into the dry grass.
senses.exampleCN: 那头鹿淡黄褐色的毛皮与枯草融为一体。
senses.why: A second word, fealu, meant pale yellow-brown and described the coat of deer, so the colour sense is a homonym that merged in spelling.
senses.whyCN: 另一个词 fealu 意为淡黄褐色，用来描写鹿的毛色，所以颜色义项是同音词在拼写上合流的结果。

senses.title: Unused potential
senses.definition: describes an ability or resource that is not being used but is still there
senses.definitionCN: 指能力或资源暂未使用，但仍然存在
senses.example: His gift for languages lay fallow during the long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 在长期患病期间，他的语言天赋一直闲置着。
senses.why: Land that is unused but not ruined suggests ability that is unused but still there.
senses.whyCN: 闲置却未被毁掉的土地，让人想到尚未使用却仍然存在的能力。

intro.en: Fallow is two Old English words in one spelling: fealh, land ploughed and left unsown, and fealu, pale yellow-brown. The colour word goes back to a reconstructed pale root shared with Latin pallere.
intro.cn: fallow 是拼写相同、来源不同的两个古英语词：fealh（翻耕后闲置的土地）与 fealu（淡黄褐色）。颜色词可追溯到意为「苍白」的构拟词根，与拉丁语 pallere 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning pale is behind the colour word; the form is written with an asterisk because it is not attested.
items.cn: 颜色词背后有一个意为「苍白」的构拟词根；因未见文献实证，学界以星号标写。

items.en: Falwaz means pale yellow, and falhaz means fallow land; the two words are distinct from the start.
items.cn: falwaz 意为淡黄色，falhaz 意为休耕的土地；两个词从一开始就彼此独立。

items.en: Fealu means pale yellow-brown, and fealh means fallow land.
items.cn: fealu 意为淡黄褐色，fealh 意为休耕地。

items.en: Falow and fallow settle into one spelling, and the two senses are felt as one word.
items.cn: falow 与 fallow 逐渐固定为一种拼写，两个义项被当作同一个词。

items.en: Fallow land, fallow deer, and a fallow period keep both the farming and the colour sense alive.
items.cn: 休耕地、淡黄褐色的鹿与停滞期，让农耕义和颜色义都继续存活。

note.en: Fallow keeps a small family of English derivatives, and its two senses sit beside words for resting land and for inactivity.
note.cn: fallow 有一小族英语派生词；它的两个义项分别靠近「歇着的土地」与「停止活动」两类词。

entries.definitionCN: 休耕状态；闲置（由 fallow 加 -ness 构成）

entries.definition: the act of leaving land fallow
entries.definitionCN: 休耕；让土地休闲（由 fallow 加 -ing 构成）

entries.definition: a deer with a pale brown coat
entries.definitionCN: 毛色淡黄的鹿（fallow 与 deer 构成的复合词）

entries.definition: not in use or not working

normalIntro.en: Fallow is a farming word with two branches: land at rest, and a pale brown colour that survives in fallow deer.
normalIntro.cn: fallow 是农耕词，长着两条枝：歇着的土地，以及在 fallow deer 中留存的淡黄褐色。

normal.en: Fallow land is land left without a crop.
normal.cn: 休耕的土地就是不种作物的地。

normal.en: To lie fallow is to rest for a season.
normal.cn: lie fallow 就是歇上一季。

normal.en: A fallow year is a year with no harvest.
normal.cn: fallow year 是没有收成的一年。

normal.en: Fallow deer carry the pale brown colour sense.
normal.cn: fallow deer 保留了淡黄褐色这一颜色义。

normal.en: Fallowness is the state of being unused.
normal.cn: fallowness 是闲置不用的状态。

abstract.en: Picture stubble and clover on a field with no crop.
abstract.cn: 想象一块没有庄稼、只有茬子和三叶草的田。

abstract.en: Picture a blank square on a map of fields.
abstract.cn: 想象田地图上的一块空白方格。

abstract.en: Picture a clock stopped for a whole season.
abstract.cn: 想象一只停走了一整季的钟。

examples.en: Half the farm lay fallow while the soil recovered.
examples.cn: 农场有一半土地休耕，让土壤恢复。

examples.en: The fallow was sown with clover to feed the bees.
examples.cn: 那块休耕地种上了三叶草，供蜜蜂采蜜。

examples.en: Her writing talent stayed fallow for almost ten years.
examples.cn: 她的写作天赋闲置了近十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法洛」——法洛的田空着一季，让草和泥土歇口气；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: fallow 由两个古英语词合流：表「休耕地」的 fealh，与表「淡黄褐色」的 fealu；后者出自原始日耳曼语 falwaz，可追溯到意为「苍白」的构拟词根，与拉丁语 pallere（苍白）同源。

sensesIntro.en: Fallow starts with resting land, becomes the land itself, then any dormant period; a homonym adds the pale brown colour, and the resting field finally yields unused potential.
sensesIntro.cn: fallow 从歇着的土地出发，先是土地本身，再指任何停滞的时期；同音词带来淡黄褐色一义，而歇着的田最后引申为闲置未用的潜力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field with no crop, resting under the sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块没有庄稼、在阳光下歇着的田。

branches.en: Land left unsown is the farming sense.
branches.cn: 闲置不种的土地是农耕义项。

branches.en: The noun names the piece of land itself.
branches.cn: 名词直接指那块土地。

branches.en: A resting field becomes any dormant period.
branches.cn: 歇着的田变成任何停滞的时期。

branches.en: The colour sense comes from a separate homonym.
branches.cn: 颜色义项来自另一个同音词。

branches.en: Unused land models unused ability and renewal.
branches.cn: 闲置的土地是闲置能力与恢复的模型。

intro.en: Fallow joins two Old English words: fealh, resting land, and fealu, pale yellow-brown; the colour word is the one with a clear Indo-European pedigree.
intro.cn: fallow 由两个古英语词合流：fealh（休耕的土地）与 fealu（淡黄褐色）；其中颜色词有清楚的印欧来源。

latinIntro.en: The colour branch goes back to a reconstructed root meaning pale, and Latin pallere, to be pale, with pallidus, pale, is a distant cousin rather than a direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 颜色这一支可追溯到意为「苍白」的构拟词根；拉丁语 pallere（苍白）与 pallidus（苍白的）是远亲，而不是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: fallow 今天兼有这两个义项。

items.example: Fallow land is the common farming phrase.
items.exampleCN: fallow land 是常见的农耕说法。
后缀 -ness 构成抽象名词。

items.example: Pale belongs to the same colour field.
items.exampleCN: pale 属于同一个颜色义场。

items.example: Pallere is a distant Latin cousin of fealu.
items.exampleCN: pallere 是 fealu 的拉丁远亲。

definition_zh: 使熟悉；使了解；熟悉起来；使普及；使习惯
definition_en: to make someone familiar with something; to get to know something oneself; to bring something into general knowledge
core_image: 老师带着新生走过一间间教室，把路和门记熟
scene: 新生入学第一天，老师带着大家走遍校园，熟悉每一间教室。On the first day, the teacher walked the new students around the campus to familiarise them with every classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 familiarise 是「使熟悉」（第 1 个义项：让人对某事物有所了解）；句意：开学第一天，老师带新生走遍校园，让他们熟悉每一间教室。

pos.zh: 使熟悉；使了解；熟悉起来

derivatives.zh: 熟悉；普及（familiarise 加 -ation 构成过程名词）
熟悉；亲近（familiar 加 -ity 构成抽象名词）
熟悉的；常见的（动词所由构成的形容词）
不熟悉的（familiar 加否定前缀 un- 构成）

senses.title: To make someone know something
senses.definition: to make a person learn about something so that it no longer feels strange
senses.definitionCN: 让某人了解某事物，使它不再陌生
senses.example: The nurse familiarised the family with the ward routines.
senses.exampleCN: 护士让家属熟悉了病房的日常流程。
senses.why: Latin familiaris meant of the household, so to familiarise is to bring something inside the circle of the known.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 familiaris 意为「家里的」，所以「使熟悉」就是把某物带进已知的圈子里。

senses.title: To get to know something oneself
senses.definition: to learn about something yourself, often with oneself as the object
senses.definitionCN: 自己动手了解某事物，常以自身为宾语
senses.example: I familiarised myself with the map before setting out.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前我先让自己熟悉了地图。
senses.why: The same verb turns reflexive: a person can bring himself or herself into that circle.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词可以反身使用：人也能把自己带进那个圈子。

senses.title: To bring into common knowledge
senses.definition: to make something known to many people so that it becomes ordinary
senses.definitionCN: 让许多人知道某事物，使它变得平常
senses.example: The posters familiarised the town with the new recycling rules.
senses.exampleCN: 那些海报让全镇熟悉了新的回收规定。
senses.why: If a thing can be made familiar to one person, it can be made familiar to many, which yields the sense of spreading knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 既然能让一个人熟悉，也就能让许多人熟悉，于是产生「普及知识」这一义项。

senses.title: To accustom an animal
senses.definition: to accustom an animal to people or to a new environment
senses.definitionCN: 让动物习惯人或者新环境
senses.example: The trainer familiarised the puppy with crowded streets.
senses.exampleCN: 训练员让小狗习惯了拥挤的街道。
senses.why: An animal can be brought into the human household in the same way, so the verb also means to tame or accustom.
senses.whyCN: 动物也能以同样的方式被带进人的家户，所以这个动词也有「驯化、使习惯」的意思。

intro.en: Familiarise is the verb of the familiar family, from Latin familia, a household, through familiaris, of the household. English added the verb suffix -ise in the modern period.
intro.cn: familiarise 是 familiar 词族的动词，源头是拉丁语 familia（家庭、家户），经 familiaris（家里的）而来；英语在近代给它加上动词后缀 -ise。

items.en: Familia means a household, including the servants of the house, and it comes from famulus, a servant.
items.cn: familia 意为家户，包括家中的仆役，源自 famulus（仆人）。

items.en: Familiaris means of the household, and so intimate or well known.
items.cn: familiaris 意为家里的，因而也表示亲近、熟知。

items.en: Familier carries the sense of intimate into Old French.
items.cn: familier 把「亲近」的含义带进古法语。

items.en: Familiar arrives in English as an adjective meaning close or well known.
items.cn: familiar 以形容词身份进入英语，意为亲近或熟知的。

items.en: The verb familiarize appears, meaning to make something well known.
items.cn: 动词 familiarize 出现，意为使某物被人们熟知。

items.en: British spelling prefers familiarise, while American spelling keeps familiarize.
items.cn: 英式拼写用 familiarise，美式拼写保留 familiarize。

note.en: Familiarise belongs to the familiar family, and its meaning neighbours verbs for getting used to people, places, and routines.
note.cn: familiarise 属于 familiar 词族，意义上与「对人、地、事变得习惯」的一类动词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 熟悉；亲近（由 familiar 加 -ity 构成）
熟悉的；常见的（动词所由构成的形容词）
使熟悉的过程（由 familiarise 加 -ation 构成）

entries.definition: to make someone know a person or thing
to make someone used to something
to make someone or something used to a condition

normalIntro.en: Familiarise is the verb of the familiar family, built with the suffix -ise: familiar plus -ise makes the act of bringing something into the known.
normalIntro.cn: familiarise 是 familiar 词族的动词，由后缀 -ise 构成：familiar 加 -ise，就是「把某物带进已知范围」的动作。

normal.en: Familiarise is familiar plus the verb suffix -ise.
normal.cn: familiarise 是 familiar 加动词后缀 -ise。

normal.en: Familiarise yourself with the rules before you start.
normal.cn: 开始前先让自己熟悉规则。

normal.en: A teacher familiarises new students with the building.
normal.cn: 老师让新生熟悉这栋楼。

normal.en: Familiarisation is the noun for that process.
normal.cn: familiarisation 是这个过程的名称。

normal.en: British spelling is familiarise, American spelling is familiarize.
normal.cn: 英式拼写是 familiarise，美式拼写是 familiarize。

abstract.en: Picture a guide opening every door for a newcomer.
abstract.cn: 想象向导为初来者打开一扇扇门。

abstract.en: Picture a finger tracing a map until the route is known.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在地图上划过，直到路线变熟。

abstract.en: Picture the same poster on every wall until the word is ordinary.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的海报贴满每一面墙，那个词就变得平常了。

examples.en: The officer familiarised the recruits with the new rules.
examples.cn: 军官让新兵熟悉了新规定。

examples.en: He familiarised himself with the machine before the shift.
examples.cn: 上班前他先让自己熟悉了这台机器。

examples.en: The museum familiarises children with ancient tools.
examples.cn: 博物馆让孩子们熟悉古代的器具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发米利爱斯」——一家人天天见面，彼此就熟悉了；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 familia（家庭、家户，源自 famulus「仆人」）→ familiaris（家里的、亲近的）→ 古法语 familier → 英语 familiar → familiarise（加 -ise 的动词）。

sensesIntro.en: Familiarise begins with making someone know a thing, turns reflexive for getting to know it oneself, widens to making it known to many, and ends with accustoming an animal.
sensesIntro.cn: familiarise 先指让人了解某物，再反身指自己去了解，随后扩展到让许多人知晓，最后落在使动物习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guide walking a newcomer through every room of a house.
core.cn: 核心意象：向导带着初来者走遍一栋房子的每间屋。

branches.en: Making someone know a thing is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 让别人了解某物是基本义项。

branches.en: The reflexive use means getting to know it oneself.
branches.cn: 反身用法指自己去了解。

branches.en: Widening the circle yields the sense of spreading knowledge.
branches.cn: 把圈子扩大，就得到普及知识这一义项。

branches.en: An animal brought into the household is accustomed to people.
branches.cn: 被带进家户的动物会习惯人。

branches.en: Both directions of the verb share the image of entering a known circle.
branches.cn: 动词的两个方向都共享「进入已知圈子」的意象。

intro.en: Familiarise grows from Latin familia, a household, through familiaris, of the household; English adds the verb suffix -ise and the nouns familiarity and familiarisation.
intro.cn: familiarise 由拉丁语 familia（家庭）经 familiaris（家里的、亲近的）长成；英语再加动词后缀 -ise，以及 familiarity、familiarisation 等名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin familia means household or family, and familiaris means belonging to the household, hence intimate and well known.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 familia 意为家户或家庭，familiaris 意为属于家户的，因而引申为亲近、熟知。

items.exampleCN: famulus 是 familia 的词源。

items.example: The suffix -ise forms verbs such as familiarise.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 构成 familiarise 这类动词。
familiarise 是这一族的中心动词。
前缀 un- 构成 unfamiliar。

definition_zh: 家庭；家族；科
definition_en: a group of parents and children, a line of relatives, or a group in biology
core_image: 周末的餐桌上，几代人围坐在一起，笑声不断
scene: 周末，一家人围坐在餐桌旁吃饭。The whole family sat around the table for dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 family 是「家庭」（第 1 个义项）；句意：全家人围坐桌旁吃晚饭。

senses.title: Parents and children
senses.definition: a group made up of parents and their children
senses.definitionCN: 由父母及其子女组成的群体
senses.example: The family eats dinner together every night.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人每晚一起吃晚饭。
senses.why: The core sense is the household of parents and children.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是父母与子女组成的家庭。

senses.title: Line of relatives
senses.definition: all the people related to one another across generations
senses.definitionCN: 跨世代相互有亲缘关系的所有人
senses.example: The family has lived here for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家族在这里住了几个世纪。
senses.why: The household extends into a line of ancestors and relatives.
senses.whyCN: 家庭扩展为祖先与亲属的血脉。

senses.title: Biological group
senses.definition: a group of related plants or animals above genus and below order
senses.definitionCN: 亲缘植物或动物的分类单元，位于属之上、目之下
senses.example: The rose belongs to the rose family.
senses.exampleCN: 玫瑰属于蔷薇科。
senses.why: Related species form a kind of family tree.
senses.whyCN: 相关物种形成一种家族树。

senses.title: Language group
senses.definition: a group of languages that developed from a common ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 由共同祖语发展而来的一组语言
senses.example: French and Spanish belong to the same language family.
senses.exampleCN: 法语和西班牙语属于同一语族。
senses.why: Languages also have parents and descendants.
senses.whyCN: 语言也有父母与后代。

intro.en: Family comes from Latin familia, a household, which included servants as well as relatives.
intro.cn: family 源自拉丁语 familia（家户），既包括亲属也包括仆役。

items.en: Famulus meant a servant or household member.
items.cn: famulus 意为仆役或家户成员。

items.en: Familia meant the whole household.
items.cn: familia 意为整个家户。

items.en: Famille narrowed to parents, children, and relatives.
items.cn: famille 缩小为父母、子女与亲属。

items.en: Family named a household and a line of descent.
items.cn: family 指家户与血统世系。

items.en: Science borrowed family for related species.
items.cn: 科学借 family 表示相关物种。

items.en: Family now covers households, relatives, and groups.
items.cn: 现代英语中 family 涵盖家庭、亲属与分类群。

note.en: Family is compared with similar spellings and with words for households and relatives.
note.cn: 把 family 与形近词以及表示家庭和亲属的词作比较。

entries.definition: all the people living in one house
people connected by blood or marriage
a large group of related families

normalIntro.en: Family begins with fam, like familiar, because family are the people we know best.
normalIntro.cn: family 以 fam 开头，像 familiar，因为家人是我们最熟悉的人。

normal.en: Family and familiar share fam, the people closest to us.
normal.cn: family 与 familiar 共享 fam，都是最亲近的人。

normal.en: The plural families changes y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数 families 要把 y 变成 ies。

normal.en: Family name is another way to say surname.
normal.cn: family name 是姓氏的另一种说法。

normal.en: A family tree shows how relatives connect.
normal.cn: 家谱树显示亲属如何相连。

normal.en: In biology, a family sits above genus and below order.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，科位于属之上、目之下。

abstract.en: Family is the first group that teaches us who we are.
abstract.cn: 家庭是第一个教我们认识自己的群体。

abstract.en: The word once meant a whole household, servants included.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指包括仆役在内的整个家户。

abstract.en: Every field has families, from roses to languages.
abstract.cn: 从玫瑰到语言，每个领域都有「科」或「语族」。

examples.en: Her family moved to the city last year.
examples.cn: 她家去年搬到了城里。

examples.en: The whole family gathers at the grandparents' house.
examples.cn: 全家人聚在祖父母家。

examples.en: The cat is a member of the cat family.
examples.cn: 猫是猫科动物的一员。

dict_mnemonic.text: family 与 familiar 都含 fam，家人是最熟悉的人；此外科学分类中的「科」和语言学的「语族」也用 family。

root: 源自拉丁语 familia（家户），更早与 famulus（仆役）相关，核心义「共同生活、相互关联的一群人」。

sensesIntro.en: Family means parents and children, a line of relatives, a biological family, or a language family.
sensesIntro.cn: family 意为父母子女组成的家庭、家族亲属、生物分类的科，或语族。

core.en: A group joined by household or descent.
core.cn: 由共同生活或血统连接的一群。

branches.en: The everyday household of parents and children.
branches.cn: 父母子女的日常家庭。

branches.en: The wider line of relatives across generations.
branches.cn: 跨世代的更广泛亲属血脉。

branches.en: Related species grouped in biology.
branches.cn: 生物学中归为一类的相关物种。

branches.en: Related languages grouped by common origin.
branches.cn: 按共同来源归类的相关语言。

branches.en: The household is the nearest part of the wider family.
branches.cn: 家庭是更大亲属范围中最近的一环。

intro.en: Family forms adjectives about home life and suitability.
intro.cn: family 构成表示家庭生活和适用性的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin familia and famulus lie behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 familia 与 famulus 是英语 family 的来源。

items.meaning: a group of parents and children

items.exampleCN: 他们买了一个家庭装披萨。
这家酒店适合家庭入住。

items.example: Family life is important to them.
items.exampleCN: 家庭生活对他们很重要。

definition_zh: 饥荒；饥饿；严重的缺乏
definition_en: a serious lack of food over a wide area, or a severe shortage of something
core_image: 干裂的土地上，空荡的粮仓和排队领粥的人群
scene: 连年干旱后，村庄陷入饥荒。After years of drought, the village faced famine.
sceneCN: 这里 famine 是「饥荒」（第 1 个义项）；句意：连年干旱后，村庄面临饥荒。

senses.title: Widespread starvation
senses.definition: a serious lack of food over a wide area, causing many deaths
senses.definitionCN: 大范围严重缺粮，导致大量死亡
senses.example: The famine killed thousands of people.
senses.exampleCN: 这场饥荒夺去了数千人的生命。
senses.why: The core sense is mass hunger caused by missing food.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是食物短缺造成的大规模饥饿。

senses.title: Hunger and food shortage
senses.definition: the state of being extremely hungry because food is unavailable
senses.definitionCN: 因没有食物而极度饥饿的状态
senses.example: The animals died during the winter famine.
senses.exampleCN: 动物在冬季缺粮时死去。
senses.why: The event is felt as hunger by those inside it.
senses.whyCN: 身处其中的人把这一事件感受为饥饿。

senses.title: Severe shortage
senses.definition: an extreme scarcity of something other than food
senses.definitionCN: 除食物之外某物的极度稀缺
senses.example: Critics spoke of a famine of good ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者谈到好想法的严重匮乏。
senses.why: The image of empty granaries extends to other shortages.
senses.whyCN: 空粮仓的意象扩展到其他短缺。

intro.en: Famine comes from Latin fames, hunger, through Old French famine.
intro.cn: famine 经古法语 famine 源自拉丁语 fames（饥饿）。

items.en: Fames means hunger.
items.cn: fames 意为饥饿。

items.en: Famelicus means hungry or starving.
items.cn: famelicus 意为饥饿的、挨饿的。

items.en: Famine named a great shortage of food.
items.cn: famine 指严重的食物短缺。

items.en: Famine entered English as widespread starvation.
items.cn: famine 以大范围饥荒之义进入英语。

items.en: Famine also describes severe shortages of other things.
items.cn: 现代英语中 famine 也形容其他事物的严重短缺。

note.en: Famine is compared with similar spellings and with words for hunger and shortage.
note.cn: 把 famine 与形近词以及表示饥饿和短缺的词作比较。

entries.definition: suffering or death from lack of food

normalIntro.en: Famine sounds like famous minus the last syllable, and famous people never face it.
normalIntro.cn: famine 像去掉末音节的 famous，而名人们不会遭遇饥荒。

normal.en: Famine and famished share the idea of extreme hunger.
normal.cn: famine 与 famished 都含极度饥饿之意。

normal.en: A famine leaves empty granaries and empty plates.
normal.cn: 饥荒留下空粮仓和空盘子。

normal.en: Drought often comes before famine.
normal.cn: 干旱常常先于饥荒出现。

normal.en: Famine relief is aid sent to hungry people.
normal.cn: famine relief 是送往饥饿人群的援助。

normal.en: The plural famines refers to several periods of hunger.
normal.cn: 复数 famines 指多个饥荒时期。

abstract.en: Famine is not only missing food but broken distribution.
abstract.cn: 饥荒不只是缺粮，也是分配失灵。

abstract.en: A rich world can still suffer a famine of care.
abstract.cn: 富足的世界仍可能缺乏关怀。

abstract.en: The word turns an empty field into a human disaster.
abstract.cn: 这个词把空荡的田地变成人间灾难。

examples.en: The country suffered a famine after the harvest failed.
examples.cn: 收成失败后，这个国家遭遇了饥荒。

examples.en: Aid workers brought food to the famine victims.
examples.cn: 救援人员给饥荒灾民送去食物。

examples.en: The report warned of a famine of affordable housing.
examples.cn: 报告警告可负担住房严重匮乏。

dict_mnemonic.text: famine 与 famished（饿极的）同族，核心是「吃不上饭」；一场大范围缺粮就是饥荒。

root: 源自拉丁语 fames（饥饿），经古法语 famine 入英语，核心义「大范围因缺粮而挨饿」。

sensesIntro.en: Famine means widespread starvation, extreme hunger, or a severe shortage of something.
sensesIntro.cn: famine 意为大范围饥荒、极度饥饿，或某物的严重缺乏。

core.en: A large-scale lack of food causing hunger.
core.cn: 造成饥饿的大范围食物短缺。

branches.en: The core disaster of mass starvation.
branches.cn: 大规模饥饿的核心灾难。

branches.en: The felt hunger of people and animals.
branches.cn: 人与动物感受到的饥饿。

branches.en: Severe shortage extended beyond food.
branches.cn: 超出食物范围的严重短缺。

branches.en: Food shortage and felt hunger define a famine.
branches.cn: 缺粮与饥饿感共同构成饥荒。

branches.en: Both are extreme scarcity with serious results.
branches.cn: 两者都是造成严重后果的极度稀缺。

intro.en: Famine has a small family around hunger and relief.
intro.cn: famine 有一个围绕饥饿与救济的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fames, hunger, is the source of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fames（饥饿）是该词族的来源。

items.exampleCN: 该地区经历了多次饥荒。

items.example: The old text says famish the enemy.

items.exampleCN: 饥荒灾民需要干净的水。
遭受饥荒的地区需要帮助。

items.example: The agency issued a famine warning.

definition_zh: 狂热者；痴迷的人；狂热的；盲信的
definition_en: a person filled with extreme, uncritical enthusiasm for a cause or activity; also, extremely enthusiastic
core_image: 神庙前，一个人手舞足蹈，像被神灵附体，久久不肯离开
scene: 比赛结束后，球迷仍围在出口，举着同一面旗喊到半夜。The fanatic stayed outside the stadium until midnight, waving the same banner.
sceneCN: 这里 fanatic 是「狂热者」（第 1 个义项：对某件事痴迷到极点的人）；句意：那个球迷在体育场外待到半夜，一直挥着同一面旗。

pos.zh: 狂热者；痴迷的人；盲信者

derivatives.zh: fanatic 加形容词后缀 -al，义为「狂热的」
fanatical 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「狂热地」
fanatic 加名词后缀 -ism，义为「狂热主义」
fanatic 的截短形式，义为「粉丝；爱好者」

senses.title: An uncritical enthusiast
senses.definition: a person who is extremely and uncritically enthusiastic about a cause, team, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某个事业、球队或活动极度痴迷、不加深究的人
senses.example: A crowd of fanatics queued all night for the final tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 一群狂热者通宵排队，只为买到最后的票。
senses.why: Latin fanaticus described someone belonging to a temple and seemingly possessed by its god, so the word first names a person driven by irrational zeal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fanaticus 指属于神庙、仿佛被庙中神灵附体的人，所以这个词最初指被非理性狂热驱使的人。

senses.title: A blind believer
senses.definition: a person whose religious or political zeal is extreme and intolerant of doubt
senses.definitionCN: 宗教或政治热情极端、容不得怀疑的人
senses.example: Religious fanatics seized the ancient shrine.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教狂热分子占据了那座古老的圣殿。
senses.why: When the temple fervour turns toward doctrine, the same word marks a believer who will not tolerate a question.
senses.whyCN: 当神庙里的狂热转向教义，同一个词就用来指容不得疑问的盲信者。

senses.title: Extremely enthusiastic
senses.definition: showing extreme, often uncritical enthusiasm for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事表现出极度、常常不加批判的热情
senses.example: Her fanatic devotion to the club surprised even her friends.
senses.exampleCN: 她对俱乐部的狂热忠诚连朋友都吃惊。
senses.why: The adjective simply carries the noun image into description: a person whose whole attention is possessed by one object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是把名词的画面带进描述：一个人的全部注意力被同一个对象占据。

senses.title: Keen on something, informally
senses.definition: very keen on or devoted to a particular pastime, used in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指非常喜欢或投入某项消遣
senses.example: My brother is fanatic about football statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟对足球数据着迷。
senses.why: Everyday speech softened the religious edge, so the word now also covers harmless obsessions such as sport or diet.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语磨掉了宗教锋芒，这个词于是也能指运动、饮食之类无害的痴迷。

intro.en: Fanatic comes from Latin fanaticus, of a temple, from fanum, a temple; the word travelled through French fanatique into English.
intro.cn: fanatic 源自拉丁语 fanaticus（神庙的），来自 fanum（神庙），经法语 fanatique 进入英语。

items.en: Fanum means a temple or a consecrated place.
items.cn: fanum 意为神庙或圣地。

items.en: Fanaticus means belonging to a temple or inspired by a god.
items.cn: fanaticus 意为属于神庙的、受神灵启发的。

items.en: Fanaticus also names a person in frantic, possessed agitation.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，fanaticus 也指狂乱、像被附体的人。

items.en: Fanatique carries the sense of frenzied religious zeal.
items.cn: fanatique 带有宗教狂热的意味。

items.en: English fanatic first labels religious dissenters who seemed possessed by zeal.
items.cn: 英语 fanatic 最初指显得狂热附体的宗教异见者。

items.en: The sense widens to sports, hobbies, and everyday enthusiasts.
items.cn: 词义随后扩展到体育、爱好和日常的痴迷者。

note.en: Fanatic sits in a family of zeal words: its adjective, its abstract noun, and a clipped everyday form, next to zealot and enthusiast.
note.cn: fanatic 处在表示「狂热」的词族里：有形容词、抽象名词和截短的口语形式，旁边是 zealot 与 enthusiast。

entries.definitionCN: 狂热的；常指不加批判的

entries.definition: a keen supporter of a team or performer
entries.definitionCN: 粉丝；影迷（fanatic 的截短形式）

entries.definition: a person with extreme political or religious zeal
a person who is very interested in an activity
a person who holds extreme views

normalIntro.en: Fanatic is built on fanum, a temple: the original fanatic was a person whose devotion looked like divine possession.
normalIntro.cn: fanatic 的词根是 fanum（神庙）：最初的 fanatic 指虔诚得像被神灵附体的人。

normal.en: Fanum is Latin for a temple, so a fanatic was first a temple-haunted person.
normal.cn: fanum 在拉丁语中指神庙，所以 fanatic 最初是个被神庙附体的人。

normal.en: The adjective fanatical and the adverb fanatically keep the same root.
normal.cn: 形容词 fanatical 与副词 fanatically 保留同一个词根。

normal.en: Fanaticism names the abstract force, while a fanatic is the person who carries it.
normal.cn: fanaticism 指这种抽象的力量，fanatic 则是承载它的那个人。

normal.en: The collocations run from a fanatic supporter to a religious fanatic to a health fanatic.
normal.cn: 搭配从「fanatic supporter」到「religious fanatic」，再到「health fanatic」，范围很清楚。

normal.en: Compare fanatic with fan: the short form has lost the hard edge and simply means a keen supporter.
normal.cn: 对比 fanatic 与 fan：截短形式磨掉了尖锐意味，只表示热心的支持者。

abstract.en: Picture a man dancing before a temple gate, unable to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在神庙门前不停手舞足蹈。

abstract.en: Picture a believer who shuts the door on every question.
abstract.cn: 想象一个信徒把所有疑问都关在门外。

abstract.en: Picture a single spotlight following one person through a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一束追光在暗厅里只跟着一个人。

examples.en: The fanatics camped outside the box office for two nights.
examples.cn: 那些狂热者在售票处外露宿了两夜。

examples.en: His fanatic loyalty to the old club never wavered.
examples.cn: 他对那家老牌俱乐部的狂热忠诚从未动摇。

examples.en: She is fanatic about keeping her garden free of weeds.
examples.cn: 她对清除花园杂草这件事非常痴迷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发奈提克」——像一个人喊到嗓子发烫也不肯停，越喊越来劲；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fanum（神庙）→ fanaticus（属于神庙的、受神灵启发的）→ 法语 fanatique → 英语 fanatic，核心义「被一股超乎常人的热情占据」。

sensesIntro.en: Fanatic starts as a person possessed by temple zeal, narrows to the blind religious or political believer, then widens into the adjective for any extreme enthusiasm, including harmless hobbies.
sensesIntro.cn: fanatic 最初指被神庙式狂热占据的人，后收窄为宗教或政治上的盲信者，再扩展为形容词，指任何一种极端热情，也包括无害的爱好。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure dancing before a temple, possessed by a power that will not let go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在神庙前手舞足蹈，被一股不肯放手的力占据。

branches.en: The possessed enthusiast is the founding sense.
branches.cn: 被附体般的痴迷者是本义。

branches.en: Blind belief is the disapproving religious or political branch.
branches.cn: 盲信是带贬义的宗教或政治分支。

branches.en: The adjective describes the same intensity as a quality.
branches.cn: 形容词把同样的强度写成一种性质。

branches.en: Informal use shrinks the zeal to a harmless pastime.
branches.cn: 非正式用法把狂热缩小为无害的消遣。

branches.en: Person and quality share one image: attention seized by a single object.
branches.cn: 人与性质共享同一画面：注意力被单一对象攫住。

intro.en: Fanatic is built on the Latin temple word fanum, with the adjective suffix -aticus; English adds -al, -ally, and -ism.
intro.cn: fanatic 建立在拉丁语神庙词 fanum 之上，带形容词后缀 -aticus；英语再加 -al、-ally 与 -ism。

latinIntro.en: Latin fanum means a temple, and fanaticus means of a temple or god-inspired.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fanum 意为神庙，fanaticus 意为神庙的、受神灵启发的。

items.example: Fanum is the root that gives the word its temple image.
items.exampleCN: fanum 是赋予这个词神庙意象的词根。

items.meaningCN: 神庙的；受神灵启发的；狂乱的
items.example: Fanaticus first described a person touched by a god.
items.exampleCN: fanaticus 最初形容被神灵触碰的人。

items.example: The suffix -aticus turns fanum into fanaticus.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -aticus 把 fanum 变成 fanaticus。

items.example: French fanatique carries the word across the Channel.
items.exampleCN: 法语 fanatique 把这个词带过海峡。

items.example: Fanatic keeps both the noun and adjective uses.
items.exampleCN: fanatic 同时保留名词与形容词用法。

items.example: Fanatical describes the intensity as a quality.
items.exampleCN: fanatical 把这种强度描述为一种性质。

items.example: Fan is fanatic clipped short in ordinary speech.
items.exampleCN: fan 是 fanatic 在日常口语中的截短形式。

definition_zh: 狂热主义；盲目的狂热；狂信
definition_en: extreme and uncritical zeal for a cause, religion, or belief
core_image: 一群人围着一座神像越挤越紧，谁也不肯回头
scene: 会场里，口号一浪高过一浪，没有人再提出疑问。The fanaticism of the crowd silenced every voice of doubt.
sceneCN: 这里 fanaticism 是「狂热的情绪」（第 1 个义项：一群人共有的盲目热情）；句意：人群的狂热压住了每一个怀疑的声音。

pos.zh: 狂热主义；盲目的狂热；狂信

derivatives.zh: fanaticism 的词干，义为「狂热者」

senses.title: A system of uncritical zeal
senses.definition: extreme and uncritical enthusiasm held as a system or shared belief
senses.definitionCN: 作为一套体系或共同信念而持有的极端、不加批判的热情
senses.example: Religious fanaticism has fueled wars for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教狂热主义数百年来为战争推波助澜。
senses.why: The suffix -ism turns the person fanatic into the abstract system of zeal itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 把「人」fanatic 变成「主义」：狂热本身成了一套被坚持的东西。

senses.title: The conduct of a fanatic
senses.definition: the behaviour or attitude of someone who pursues an activity with extreme devotion
senses.definitionCN: 以极端投入从事某项活动的人所表现出的行为或态度
senses.example: His fanaticism about training left no room for rest.
senses.exampleCN: 他对训练的狂热让休息没有容身之地。
senses.why: The abstract noun can also name the daily conduct that such zeal produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个抽象名词也能指这种狂热在日常生活里造成的行为。

senses.title: Intolerance of other beliefs
senses.definition: intolerant devotion that refuses to consider any other view
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝考虑任何其他观点的、不容异见的投入
senses.example: Fanaticism closes the door on every compromise.
senses.exampleCN: 狂热主义对一切妥协都关上了门。
senses.why: When zeal hardens into certainty, the word carries a strong note of intolerance.
senses.whyCN: 当狂热硬化成「确定无疑」，这个词就带上了强烈的不容异见色彩。

intro.en: Fanaticism is fanatic plus the Latin suffix -ismus, which names a system, practice, or condition.
intro.cn: fanaticism 由 fanatic 加拉丁语后缀 -ismus 构成，该后缀表示体系、做法或状态。

items.en: The suffix -ismos names a practice, doctrine, or habit of a group.
items.cn: 后缀 -ismos 指一种做法、教义或群体的习性。

items.en: -ismus is the Latin form of the Greek suffix.
items.cn: -ismus 是这个希腊语后缀的拉丁语形式。

items.en: Fanaticus supplies the temple-zeal image behind the word.
items.cn: fanaticus 提供这个词背后的神庙狂热意象。

items.en: Fanatisme names religious frenzy before the English form spreads.
items.cn: fanatisme 在英语形式传播之前就指宗教狂热。

items.en: English adopts fanaticism during the age of religious controversy.
items.cn: 英语在宗教论争的时代吸收了 fanaticism。

items.en: The word extends from religion to politics, sport, and other causes.
items.cn: 这个词从宗教扩展到政治、体育和其他事业。

note.en: Fanaticism is the abstract noun beside fanatic, and it borders on words for intolerance and single-minded devotion.
note.cn: fanaticism 是与 fanatic 相对的抽象名词，并与表示不容异见和一味投入的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Fanaticism is fanatic plus -ism: the person becomes a system, a habit of mind shared by a group.
normalIntro.cn: fanaticism 是 fanatic 加 -ism：人变成一套体系，一种被群体共享的心态。

normal.en: -ism turns a person into an abstract force: fanatic gives fanaticism.
normal.cn: 「-ism」把人变成抽象力量：fanatic 加 -ism 就是 fanaticism。

normal.en: The same -ism appears in realism, criticism, and optimism.
normal.cn: 同一个「-ism」也出现在「realism」「criticism」与「optimism」里。

normal.en: Religious fanaticism, political fanaticism, sports fanaticism: one pattern covers them all.
normal.cn: 宗教狂热、政治狂热、体育狂热，都由同一个模式覆盖。

normal.en: Fanaticism is uncritical: it repeats a belief and refuses to test it.
normal.cn: fanaticism 是不加批判的：它重复一个信念，拒绝检验它。

normal.en: Compare fanatic, the person, with fanaticism, the climate that produces such people.
normal.cn: 对比 fanatic 这个人与 fanaticism 这种造就此类人的氛围。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pushing toward one statue until the exits are blocked.
abstract.cn: 想象人群朝一座神像越挤越紧，把出口都堵住。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who ignores a torn muscle and keeps going.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者不顾拉伤的肌肉继续跑。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every window is sealed and one lamp burns.
abstract.cn: 想象一间封死所有窗户、只点一盏灯的房间。

examples.en: Religious fanaticism lay behind the destruction of the old shrine.
examples.cn: 宗教狂热是那座古殿被毁的深层原因。

examples.en: His fanaticism about diet turned a simple meal into a ritual.
examples.cn: 他对饮食的狂热把一顿便饭变成了仪式。

examples.en: Fanaticism cannot survive a question that is honestly asked.
examples.cn: 狂热经不起一个真诚提出的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「范乃提西泽姆」——像一长串口号连喊不停，喊到没人敢插嘴；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: fanatic（狂热者，源自拉丁语 fanum 神庙 + -aticus）+ 后缀 -ism（主义、体系）→ fanaticism，核心义「把个人的狂热固化成一套集体信念」。

sensesIntro.en: Fanaticism moves from the abstract system of zeal, to the conduct of a fanatic, to the intolerance that zeal breeds.
sensesIntro.cn: fanaticism 从狂热的抽象体系，走到狂热者的行为，再到这种狂热滋生的不容异见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd pressed around one statue while every other door is sealed.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群紧围一座神像，其余的门都被封死。

branches.en: The abstract system of zeal is the core sense.
branches.cn: 狂热的抽象体系是核心义项。

branches.en: Fanatic conduct is the practical branch.
branches.cn: 狂热者的行为是实践层面的分支。

branches.en: Intolerance is the moral branch.
branches.cn: 不容异见是道德层面的分支。

branches.en: A shared system shows itself in repeated conduct.
branches.cn: 一套共享的体系会在反复的行为里显形。

branches.en: Refusing rest and refusing doubt grow from one habit.
branches.cn: 拒绝休息与拒绝怀疑出自同一种习性。

intro.en: Fanaticism is made of the fanatic stem and the suffix -ism, the English shape of Latin -ismus, which names doctrines, systems, and habits.
intro.cn: fanaticism 由 fanatic 词干与后缀 -ism 构成，后者是拉丁语 -ismus 的英语形式，用来指教义、体系与习性。

latinIntro.en: Latin -ismus comes from Greek -ismos, a suffix for practices and doctrines; it turns fanaticus into a name for a system of zeal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 -ismus 源自希腊语 -ismos，是表示做法与教义的后缀；它把 fanaticus 变成一套狂热体系的名字。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms fanaticism from fanatic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 把 fanatic 构成 fanaticism。

items.meaningCN: 希腊语 -ismos 的拉丁语形式
items.example: -ismus is the bridge between Greek and English -ism.
items.exampleCN: -ismus 是希腊语与英语 -ism 之间的桥。

items.example: Greek -ismos named the habits of a group.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 -ismos 指一个群体的习性。

items.example: Fanatic is the stem that -ism attaches to.
items.exampleCN: fanatic 是 -ism 所依附的词干。

items.example: Fanum is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: fanum 是这个词族最古老的一层。

items.example: Fanaticism and fanatical share the same stem.
items.exampleCN: fanaticism 与 fanatical 共享同一个词干。

items.example: Fanatically describes how a fanatic acts.
items.exampleCN: fanatically 描述狂热者行事的方式。

items.example: Fan is fanatic shortened in everyday speech.
items.exampleCN: fan 是 fanatic 在日常口语中的截短形式。

definition_zh: 幻想；别致的；想象的
definition_en: elaborate and decorative, imagined rather than real, or to want something
core_image: 橱窗里一条缀满亮片和蕾丝的连衣裙，精致得不太日常
scene: 她穿了一条别致的连衣裙去参加晚会。She wore a fancy dress to the party.
sceneCN: 这里 fancy 是「别致的；花哨的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她穿了一条别致的连衣裙去参加晚会。

senses.title: Elaborate and decorative
senses.definition: unusually elaborate, decorated, or complicated
senses.definitionCN: 不同寻常地精致、装饰繁复或复杂的
senses.example: The cake had fancy decorations.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上有精致的装饰。
senses.why: The core sense is more decoration than necessary.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是超出必要的装饰。

senses.title: Expensive and upscale
senses.definition: of high quality and cost, often too expensive for everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 质量与价格都高，常超出日常所需
senses.example: They ate at a fancy hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一家高档酒店用餐。
senses.why: Elaboration becomes a mark of luxury.
senses.whyCN: 精致成为奢华的标志。

senses.title: Imagination
senses.definition: the power of imagining things, or something imagined
senses.definitionCN: 想象事物的能力，或想象出的东西
senses.example: The story is a product of fancy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事是想象的产物。
senses.why: Decoration and imagination both go beyond plain fact.
senses.whyCN: 装饰与想象都超出平淡的事实。

senses.title: Want or like
senses.definition: to want something or feel like doing it, used in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 想要某物或想做某事，用于非正式英式英语
senses.example: Do you fancy a cup of tea?
senses.exampleCN: 你想喝杯茶吗？
senses.why: A passing wish is a fancy in motion.
senses.whyCN: 一时的愿望就是行动中的幻想。

intro.en: Fancy is a shortened form of fantasy, from Greek phantasia, imagination.
intro.cn: fancy 是 fantasy 的缩略形式，源自希腊语 phantasia（想象）。

items.en: Phantasia meant appearance or imagination.
items.cn: phantasia 意为显现或想象。

items.en: Phantasia meant imagination or a phantom.
items.cn: phantasia 意为想象或幻影。

items.en: Fantaisie meant imagination or a whim.
items.cn: fantaisie 意为想象或一时兴致。

items.en: Fantasie and fantsy named imagination.
items.cn: fantasie 与 fantsy 指想象力。

items.en: Fancy shortened the word and added the sense of taste.
items.cn: fancy 缩短了词形，并增加品味之义。

items.en: Fancy covers decoration, luxury, imagination, and desire.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fancy 涵盖装饰、奢华、想象与愿望。

note.en: Fancy is compared with similar spellings and with words for decoration and imagination.
note.cn: 把 fancy 与形近词以及表示装饰和想象的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fancy is fantasy shortened, so it keeps the shine of imagination.
normalIntro.cn: fancy 是 fantasy 的缩略，仍保留想象的光泽。

normal.en: Fancy is fantasy minus tasy, a quicker way to say imagination.
normal.cn: fancy 是 fantasy 去掉 tasy，是想象的快捷说法。

normal.en: Fancy dress can mean a costume or an elaborate dress.
normal.cn: fancy dress 既可指化装服，也可指别致的连衣裙。

normal.en: A fancy restaurant is expensive and decorated.
normal.cn: fancy restaurant 是高档且装饰讲究的餐厅。

normal.en: Do you fancy tea means do you want tea.
normal.cn: Do you fancy tea 意为你想喝茶吗。

normal.en: Fanciful means full of imagination.
normal.cn: fanciful 意为充满想象的。

abstract.en: Fancy is the mind adding decoration to plain reality.
abstract.cn: fancy 是心灵给平淡现实添加装饰。

abstract.en: A fancy is a wish that has not yet asked permission.
abstract.cn: 幻想是尚未征求许可的愿望。

abstract.en: The word links what looks rich with what is imagined.
abstract.cn: 这个词把看起来华丽的东西与想象之物连接起来。

examples.en: She fancied a walk along the river.
examples.cn: 她想沿河散散步。

examples.en: The shop sells fancy cakes and chocolates.
examples.cn: 这家店卖精致的蛋糕和巧克力。

examples.en: His story was pure fancy.
examples.cn: 他的故事纯属想象。

dict_mnemonic.text: fancy 是 fantasy 的缩写，本义「想象」；想象出来的东西往往花哨精致，于是又有「别致、高档」和「想要」的意思。

root: 由 fantasy 缩略而来，源自希腊语 phantasia（想象），核心义「脱离平淡现实的想象与装饰」。

sensesIntro.en: Fancy means elaborate or upscale, imagination, or to want something in informal British English.
sensesIntro.cn: fancy 意为精致花哨或高档、想象，或在非正式英式英语中表示想要。

core.en: Imagination that adds colour beyond plain fact.
core.cn: 在平淡事实之外增添色彩的想象。

branches.en: Decoration makes an object elaborate.
branches.cn: 装饰使物品变得精致。

branches.en: Elaboration becomes a sign of luxury.
branches.cn: 精致成为奢华的标志。

branches.en: The original sense of imagination remains.
branches.cn: 想象的本义仍然保留。

branches.en: A sudden wish is imagination turned toward action.
branches.cn: 一时的愿望是转向行动的想象。

branches.en: Both decoration and imagination go beyond the plain.
branches.cn: 装饰与想象都超越平淡。

intro.en: Fancy has a family of imagination and decoration.
intro.cn: fancy 有围绕想象与装饰的词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek phantasia and Latin phantasia are the distant roots.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phantasia 与拉丁语 phantasia 是远源。

items.example: It is the fanciest hotel in town.
items.exampleCN: 这是城里最高档的酒店。
她想要一个安静的夜晚。

items.example: The fanciness of the dress surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这条裙子的花哨让我们吃惊。

definition_zh: 极好的；奇异的；古怪的
definition_en: extremely good, or strange and imagined rather than real
core_image: 舞台灯光亮起，观众全体起立，为一场精彩演出欢呼
scene: 演出结束后，观众高喊太棒了。The crowd shouted that the show was fantastic.
sceneCN: 这里 fantastic 是「极好的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：观众高喊这场演出太棒了。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: extremely good or enjoyable, used in informal praise
senses.definitionCN: 极好或令人愉快的，用于非正式赞扬
senses.example: We had a fantastic time at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海滩度过了极好的时光。
senses.why: The core modern sense is strong approval.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是强烈的赞许。

senses.title: Strange and imagined
senses.definition: strange, unlikely, or produced by imagination rather than reality
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪、不太可能，或由想象而非现实产生
senses.example: The story features fantastic creatures.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里有奇异的生物。
senses.why: The older sense is something beyond the ordinary world.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的义项是超出寻常世界的事物。

senses.title: Enormously large
senses.definition: very large in amount or degree, often surprisingly so
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上非常大，常令人惊讶
senses.example: The project was a fantastic amount of work.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目的工作量大得惊人。
senses.why: What exceeds imagination also exceeds ordinary size.
senses.whyCN: 超出想象的东西也超出寻常规模。

intro.en: Fantastic comes from Greek phantastikos, able to imagine, through Latin.
intro.cn: fantastic 经拉丁语源自希腊语 phantastikos（能想象的）。

items.en: Phantastikos meant able to form images in the mind.
items.cn: phantastikos 意为能在心中形成形象的。

items.en: Phantasticus meant imaginary or unreal.
items.cn: phantasticus 意为想象中的、不真实的。

items.en: Fantastic meant existing only in imagination.
items.cn: fantastic 意为只存在于想象中的。

items.en: The word described strange and exaggerated things.
items.cn: 该词形容奇异夸张的事物。

items.en: Fantastic also became a strong word of praise.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fantastic 也成为强烈的赞美词。

note.en: Fantastic is compared with similar spellings and with words for praise and strangeness.
note.cn: 把 fantastic 与形近词以及表示赞美和奇异的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fantastic comes from fantasy, so it means both imagined wonders and real delight.
normalIntro.cn: fantastic 源自 fantasy，既指想象中的奇妙，也指现实的喜悦。

normal.en: Fantastic and fantasy share the fan sound.
normal.cn: fantastic 与 fantasy 共享 fan 的音。

normal.en: A fantastic meal is almost too good to be real.
normal.cn: 一顿极好的饭几乎好得不真实。

normal.en: Fantastic creatures belong to fantasy stories.
normal.cn: 奇异生物属于奇幻故事。

normal.en: Fantastically means in an amazing way.
normal.cn: fantastically 意为以惊人的方式。

normal.en: In speech, fantastic often simply means very good.
normal.cn: 在口语中 fantastic 常常只表示很好。

abstract.en: Fantastic things stretch what we think is possible.
abstract.cn: 奇妙之物拓展我们对可能性的认知。

abstract.en: Praise and wonder share one word.
abstract.cn: 赞美与惊奇共用一个词。

abstract.en: The word began in the mind and now describes the world.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于心灵，如今用来描述世界。

examples.en: The view from the top was fantastic.
examples.cn: 山顶的景色美极了。

examples.en: She came up with a fantastic plan.
examples.cn: 她想出了一个绝妙计划。

examples.en: The novel is full of fantastic animals.
examples.cn: 这部小说满是奇异的动物。

dict_mnemonic.text: fantastic 与 fantasy 同源，本义「只存在于想象中的」；想象中最好的东西，就是口语里的「棒极了」。

root: 源自希腊语 phantastikos（能想象的），经拉丁语 phantasticus 入英语，核心义「超出寻常、仿佛出自想象」。

sensesIntro.en: Fantastic means extremely good, strange and imagined, or surprisingly large.
sensesIntro.cn: fantastic 意为极好的、奇异想象的，或数量惊人的。

core.en: Something beyond the ordinary, whether wonderful or strange.
core.cn: 超出寻常的事物，无论美妙还是奇异。

branches.en: The modern sense of strong approval.
branches.cn: 强烈赞许的现代义。

branches.en: The older sense of strange imagination.
branches.cn: 奇异想象的古老义。

branches.en: Something so large it seems unreal.
branches.cn: 大到显得不真实的程度。

branches.en: Praise and surprise both exceed the ordinary.
branches.cn: 赞美与惊奇都超出寻常。

branches.en: Imagined things are often exaggerated in size.
branches.cn: 想象之物常在大小上被夸张。

intro.en: Fantastic belongs to the fantasy family of imagination.
intro.cn: fantastic 属于 fantasy 的想象词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek phantasia and Latin phantasticus are the roots.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phantasia 与拉丁语 phantasticus 是词根。

items.example: The fantasist created a new world.
items.exampleCN: 这位奇幻作家创造了一个新世界。

items.example: The hotel has a fantastic view.

definition_zh: 幻想；想象的产物
definition_en: a pleasant imagined situation, or a story built from imagination
core_image: 孩子躺在床上，闭眼想象自己骑着龙飞过城堡
scene: 她常常幻想自己住在海边。She often has a fantasy about living by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 fantasy 是「幻想」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她常幻想住在海边。

senses.title: Imagined situation
senses.definition: a pleasant situation that a person imagines but that is unlikely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 人想象出的愉快但不太可能发生的情境
senses.example: Winning the prize was only a fantasy.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖只是幻想。
senses.why: The core sense is a desired scene made in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是心中构建的愿望场景。

senses.title: Fantasy fiction
senses.definition: a story or genre full of magic and imaginary creatures
senses.definitionCN: 充满魔法与虚构生物的故事或文学类型
senses.example: She reads fantasy every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚读奇幻小说。
senses.why: A shared imagined world becomes a literary genre.
senses.whyCN: 共享的想象世界成为文学类型。

senses.title: Musical fantasy
senses.definition: a piece of music shaped freely by the composer's imagination
senses.definitionCN: 由作曲家想象自由构型的音乐作品
senses.example: The pianist played a fantasy by Mozart.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家演奏了一首莫扎特幻想曲。
senses.why: Free imagination shapes music as it shapes stories.
senses.whyCN: 自由想象既塑造故事也塑造音乐。

intro.en: Fantasy comes from Greek phantasia, appearance or imagination.
intro.cn: fantasy 源自希腊语 phantasia（显现、想象）。

items.en: Phantasia meant a showing or an image in the mind.
items.cn: phantasia 意为显现或心中形象。

items.en: Phantasia meant imagination or a phantom.
items.cn: phantasia 意为想象或幻影。

items.en: Fantaisie meant imagination or a whim.
items.cn: fantaisie 意为想象或一时兴致。

items.en: Fantasy named the power of imagining.
items.cn: fantasy 指想象的能力。

items.en: Fantasy became a popular genre of fiction.
items.cn: fantasy 成为流行的文学类型。

note.en: Fantasy is compared with similar spellings and with words for imagination and dreams.
note.cn: 把 fantasy 与形近词以及表示想象和梦想的词作比较。

entries.definition: the power to form mental images

normalIntro.en: Fantasy is the full form behind fancy and fantastic.
normalIntro.cn: fantasy 是 fancy 与 fantastic 背后的完整形式。

normal.en: Fantasy is the long form; fancy is the short one.
normal.cn: fantasy 是长形式，fancy 是短形式。

normal.en: Fantasy novels build worlds with magic.
normal.cn: 奇幻小说用魔法构建世界。

normal.en: A fantasy is often a wish wearing a costume.
normal.cn: 幻想常是穿着戏服的愿望。

normal.en: Fantasize is the verb form with ize.
normal.cn: fantasize 是带 ize 的动词形式。

normal.en: The plural fantasies changes y to ies.
