normal.cn: 复数 fantasies 要把 y 变成 ies。

abstract.en: Fantasy is where the mind tries on other lives.
abstract.cn: 幻想是心灵试穿他人生活的地方。

abstract.en: A shared fantasy can become a whole genre.
abstract.cn: 共享的幻想可以成为完整的文学类型。

abstract.en: Fantasy and reality need each other to be understood.
abstract.cn: 幻想与现实需要彼此才能被理解。

examples.en: He lives in a fantasy of wealth and fame.
examples.cn: 他活在名利双收的幻想中。

examples.en: The film is a fantasy set in a magic kingdom.
examples.cn: 这部电影是以魔法王国为背景的奇幻作品。

examples.en: Her childhood fantasy was to become an astronaut.
examples.cn: 她童年的幻想是成为宇航员。

dict_mnemonic.text: fantasy 是「幻想」的完整形式，fancy 是它的缩短版，fantastic 是「像幻想般奇妙」的形容词。

root: 源自希腊语 phantasia（显现、想象），核心义「在心中构建出的形象或情境」。

sensesIntro.en: Fantasy means an imagined situation, a genre of imaginative fiction, or a free musical piece.
sensesIntro.cn: fantasy 意为幻想情境、奇幻文学类型，或自由构型的幻想曲。

core.en: An imagined world built by the mind.
core.cn: 心灵构建的想象世界。

branches.en: A private imagined situation.
branches.cn: 私人的想象情境。

branches.en: An imagined world shared through fiction.
branches.cn: 通过小说共享的想象世界。

branches.en: Imagination shaping a musical piece.
branches.cn: 想象塑造的音乐作品。

branches.en: Private dreams and public stories both imagine worlds.
branches.cn: 私人梦想与公共故事都在想象世界。

branches.en: Both are creative forms built from imagination.
branches.cn: 两者都是由想象构建的创作形式。

intro.en: Fantasy has a family of verbs, writers, and adjectives.
intro.cn: fantasy 有动词、作家与形容词构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek phantasia, imagination, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phantasia（想象）是远源。

items.exampleCN: 这位奇幻作家发明了一个王国。

items.example: A fantastical castle rose above the trees.
items.exampleCN: 一座奇幻的城堡耸立在树梢之上。
这部奇幻小说卖得很好。

items.example: The game creates a fantasy world.
items.exampleCN: 游戏创造了一个幻想世界。

definition_zh: 遥远的；远方的；出神的；心不在焉的
definition_en: distant in space or time; also, dreamy and absent in expression
core_image: 一个人立在窗前，目光落在玻璃之外很远的一点
scene: 她望着窗外，眼神落在很远的地方，别人叫她也没听见。She had a faraway look, as if she were listening to a distant voice.
sceneCN: 这里 faraway 是「出神的」（第 2 个义项：心思飘远、不在此处）；句意：她眼神出神，仿佛在听一个很远处的声音。

pos.zh: 遥远的；远方的；出神的；心不在焉的

derivatives.zh: 由 far 加 off 构成的同义复合词，义为「遥远的」
faraway 的前半成分，单独使用表示「远的」
faraway 的后半成分，单独使用表示「离开；在远处」

senses.title: Distant in space
senses.definition: located or happening a long way off
senses.definitionCN: 位于或发生在很远的地方
senses.example: They set out for a faraway island before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在日出前出发，前往一座遥远的海岛。
senses.why: Faraway joins far and away, so the first sense simply puts physical distance into one word.
senses.whyCN: faraway 由 far 与 away 合成，所以第一个义项只是把物理距离装进一个词。

senses.title: Dreamy and absent
senses.definition: showing that the mind is somewhere else and not paying attention
senses.definitionCN: 显出心思在别处、没有留神的样子
senses.example: He gave a faraway smile and did not answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他出神地笑了笑，没有回答。
senses.why: A gaze fixed on something distant looks exactly like a mind that has wandered off, so distance becomes mental absence.
senses.whyCN: 目光定在远处，看上去正像心思飘走了，于是空间距离变成心神的不在场。

senses.title: Distant in time
senses.definition: belonging to a distant past or a remote memory
senses.definitionCN: 属于久远的过去或遥远的记忆
senses.example: That faraway summer still feels close to her.
senses.exampleCN: 那个久远的夏天在她心里仍然很近。
senses.why: Distance in space easily becomes distance in time, and memory inherits the same haze.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的距离很容易变成时间上的距离，记忆也继承了同样的朦胧。

senses.title: Remote in manner
senses.definition: emotionally remote, not warm or immediate in manner
senses.definitionCN: 情感上疏远，态度不温暖、不亲近
senses.example: There was a faraway courtesy in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音里有一种疏远的客气。
senses.why: A person who seems far away in thought can also seem far away in feeling.
senses.whyCN: 一个人在心思上显得很远，在情感上也会显得很远。

intro.en: Faraway is an English compound of far, from Old English feor, and away, from onweg; the two parts were written as one word in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: faraway 是英语复合词，由 far（古英语 feor，远的）与 away（古英语 onweg，离开）合成，到十九世纪才写成一个词。

items.en: Feor means far or distant.
items.cn: feor 意为远的、遥远的。

items.en: Onweg means away or from this place.
items.cn: onweg 意为离开、从这里走开。

items.en: Far and away live separate lives as adverb and adjective.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，far 与 away 各自独立使用。

items.en: The two words begin to appear as the compound far-away.
items.cn: 这两个词开始以连字符复合形式 far-away 出现。

items.en: The compound adds the mental sense of a dreamy, absent gaze.
items.cn: 这个复合词增加了「出神、心不在焉的目光」这一心理义。

items.en: Faraway now also covers distant times and remote manners.
items.cn: faraway 现在也指久远的时间和疏远的态度。

note.en: Faraway is a compound of distance; it sits near far-off and remote, and near dreamy when the distance is in the eyes.
note.cn: faraway 是一个表示距离的复合词，与 far-off、remote 相邻；当距离落在眼神里时，又与 dreamy 相邻。

entries.definition: at or to a great distance
from this place, at a distance

entries.definitionCN: 遥远的（与 faraway 同义的复合词）

entries.definition: far away, or distant in manner
far away in space or time
absorbed in thought, not fully present

normalIntro.en: Faraway is literally far plus away: two words for distance pressed into one adjective.
normalIntro.cn: faraway 字面上就是 far 加 away：两个表示距离的词压成一个形容词。

normal.en: Far gives the distance and away gives the direction, so faraway means placed at a great distance.
normal.cn: far 给距离，away 给方向，合起来就是「在很远的地方」。

normal.en: A faraway place and a faraway look use the same word for two kinds of distance.
normal.cn: 「faraway place」与「faraway look」用同一个词说两种距离。

normal.en: Compare far-off: the two compounds mean almost the same thing.
normal.cn: 对比 far-off：这两个复合词意思几乎一样。

normal.en: Faraway is written as one word, while far away stays two words for the adverbial phrase.
normal.cn: faraway 写成一个词，而副词短语「far away」仍分开写。

normal.en: The look sense grows from the place sense: the eyes are fixed on something out of reach.
normal.cn: 「出神」义从「远方」义长出来：目光落在够不到的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a boat shrinking to a dot on the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一只船在地平线上缩成一个小点。

abstract.en: Picture a window with rain running down it and nobody behind the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇雨水滑落的窗，玻璃后面没有人。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph curling at the edges, taken long ago.
abstract.cn: 想象一张边角卷起的旧照片，是很久以前拍的。

examples.en: She keeps a faraway village in her stories.
examples.cn: 她的故事里总有一个遥远的村庄。

examples.en: He stared at the rain with a faraway expression.
examples.cn: 他望着雨，神情出神。

examples.en: The letters came from a faraway country that no longer exists.
examples.cn: 那些信来自一个已不存在的远方国度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发啊喂」——站在远处喊一声「喂」，声音要拖得很长才传得到；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 far（古英语 feor，远的）+ away（古英语 onweg，离开）→ faraway，核心义「距离被拉得很远」，由空间距离引申到时间与心神。

sensesIntro.en: Faraway begins as plain physical distance, then becomes distance in time, distance in the eyes of a dreamer, and distance in manner.
sensesIntro.cn: faraway 先指单纯的空间距离，再指时间上的久远、出神者眼里的距离，以及待人接物上的疏远。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure at a window, eyes fixed on a point far beyond the glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人立在窗前，目光落在玻璃之外很远的一点。

branches.en: Physical distance is the founding sense.
branches.cn: 物理距离是本义。

branches.en: The dreamy gaze is the mental branch.
branches.cn: 出神的目光是心理层面的分支。

branches.en: Distant time is the memory branch.
branches.cn: 久远的时间是记忆层面的分支。

branches.en: Remote manner is the social branch.
branches.cn: 疏远的态度是社交层面的分支。

branches.en: The same gaze crosses space and mind: what is far outside is also far within.
branches.cn: 同一道目光穿过空间与心神：外面很远的东西，里面也很远。

intro.en: Faraway is a native English compound, not a Latin derivative: far and away are its two living parts, and far-off is its twin.
intro.cn: faraway 是英语本土复合词，并非拉丁派生词：far 与 away 是两个活着的成分，far-off 是它的孪生形式。

latinIntro.en: Faraway has no Latin root: its parts descend from Old English feor, far, and onweg, away.
latinIntro.cn: faraway 没有拉丁词根：它的成分来自古英语 feor（远的）与 onweg（离开）。

items.example: Far supplies the distance half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: far 提供这个复合词的距离部分。

items.meaning: from this place, at a distance
items.example: Away supplies the direction of the distance.
Feor is the Old English ancestor of far.
items.exampleCN: feor 是 far 的古英语祖先。

items.example: Onweg is the Old English ancestor of away.
items.exampleCN: onweg 是 away 的古英语祖先。

items.example: Afar keeps an old phrase for distance in one word.
items.exampleCN: afar 把表示距离的古老说法收进一个词。

items.example: Far-off is the twin compound of faraway.
items.exampleCN: far-off 是 faraway 的孪生复合词。

items.example: Older texts often print far-away with a hyphen.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本常把 far-away 写成带连字符的形式。

items.example: Faraway joins the two parts into one word.
items.exampleCN: faraway 把两个成分合成一个词。

definition_zh: 闹剧；荒唐事；笑剧；馅料（旧义）
definition_en: a comic play or film full of absurd situations; also, an absurd or ridiculous event
core_image: 舞台上，演员被塞进一只过大的箱子，越挣扎越好笑
scene: 会议开了三个小时，最后连主持人都笑场了。The whole hearing turned into a farce when the witness refused to answer.
sceneCN: 这里 farce 是「闹剧」（第 2 个义项：荒唐得像演戏一样的事件）；句意：证人拒绝回答，整场听证会变成了一场闹剧。

collocations.phrase: a farce from start to finish

derivatives.zh: farce 加形容词后缀 -ical，义为「闹剧般的；荒唐的」
farcical 加 -ly，义为「荒唐可笑地」
源自法语，指「闹剧作家；演闹剧的人」

senses.title: A comic stage play
senses.definition: a comic play or film that relies on absurd situations and physical humour
senses.definitionCN: 依靠荒唐情境与肢体滑稽的喜剧或喜剧片
senses.example: The actors turned the old farce into a brisk ninety-minute show.
senses.exampleCN: 演员们把那出老闹剧改成了一台轻快的九十分钟演出。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin farcire, to stuff: the play was stuffed with jokes and stage business.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 farcire（填塞）：剧本里塞满了笑料与舞台噱头。

senses.title: An absurd event
senses.definition: an event or situation so badly organized or absurd that it seems like a comedy
senses.definitionCN: 组织得极糟或荒唐到像喜剧的事件或局面
senses.example: The peace talks became a farce of postponed meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 和谈变成了一场不断延期的闹剧。
senses.why: A real event that follows a stage farce looks scripted for laughter, so the word moves from theatre to life.
senses.whyCN: 现实事件若按舞台闹剧的路数走，就像为了逗笑而写好的剧本，于是这个词从剧场走进生活。

senses.title: A hollow pretence
senses.definition: something that pretends to be serious or important but is empty or ridiculous
senses.definitionCN: 假装严肃或重要、实则空洞可笑的东西
senses.example: The inquiry was a farce that changed nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 那场调查是一场什么也没改变的闹剧。
senses.why: When a solemn form is stuffed with nothing, the word names the hollow show.
senses.whyCN: 当庄严的形式里什么也没塞进去，这个词就用来指空心的表演。

senses.title: Seasoned stuffing
senses.definition: a seasoned stuffing used to fill meat or vegetables, an older cooking sense
senses.definitionCN: 用来填进肉或蔬菜的调味馅料，是较古老的烹饪义
senses.example: The old cookbook calls the herb mixture a farce.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧菜谱把这种香草混合物叫作馅料。
senses.why: The original Latin sense was literally stuffing, and this kitchen meaning survives in old recipes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义就是填塞物，这个厨房里的意思保存在旧菜谱中。

intro.en: Farce comes from Latin farcire, to stuff, through French farce, the comic interlude stuffed into a church play.
intro.cn: farce 来自拉丁语 farcire（填塞），经法语 farce（塞进宗教剧里的滑稽插段）进入英语。

items.en: Farcire means to stuff or fill.
items.cn: farcire 意为填塞、装满。

items.en: Farcimen names stuffing, especially forcemeat.
items.cn: farcimen 指馅料，尤指剁碎的肉馅。

items.en: Farce is first a stuffing, then a comic interlude stuffed into a play.
items.cn: farce 先指馅料，后指塞进戏剧里的滑稽插段。

items.en: English farce names a comic episode inserted into a longer work.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 farce 指插进较长作品里的滑稽段落。

items.en: The word shifts from inserted comedy to the absurd event itself.
items.cn: 词义从「插入的喜剧」转向「荒唐事件本身」。

items.en: The cooking sense survives mainly in historical recipes.
items.cn: 烹饪义主要保存在历史菜谱里。

note.en: Farce began as stuffing and became both a stage comedy and a word for absurd reality; it sits near satire, mockery, and travesty.
note.cn: farce 起于「填塞」，后来既指舞台喜剧，也指荒唐的现实；它与 satire、mockery、travesty 相邻。

entries.definition: a writer or performer of farces
comedy that exposes folly or vice

entries.definitionCN: 滑稽的歪曲；拙劣的模仿

normalIntro.en: Farce began in the kitchen: farcire means to stuff, and a comic scene was stuffed into a serious play.
normalIntro.cn: farce 起于厨房：farcire 意为填塞，而滑稽场面正是被塞进严肃戏剧里的。

normal.en: Farcire, to stuff, is the root: the play is stuffed with jokes.
normal.cn: 「farcire」意为填塞，是这个词的根：剧本里被塞满笑料。

normal.en: French farce first meant stuffing and then a comic insert.
normal.cn: 法语「farce」先指馅料，后指插进戏里的滑稽段子。

normal.en: A political farce and a stage farce share the same absurd mechanics.
normal.cn: 政治闹剧与舞台闹剧共用同一套荒唐机制。

normal.en: Farcical is the adjective, farcically the adverb: the family keeps the comic note.
normal.cn: farcical 是形容词，farcically 是副词，整个词族都保留滑稽色彩。

normal.en: Compare farce with travesty: farce is absurd action, travesty is a grotesque imitation.
normal.cn: 对比 farce 与 travesty：farce 是荒唐的行动，travesty 是扭曲的模仿。

abstract.en: Picture a stage where the prop door will not close and the actor keeps stuffing it with coats.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上一扇道具门关不上，演员不断往里塞外套。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where the microphones fail one after another.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会议，麦克风一个接一个坏掉。

abstract.en: Picture a frame painted gold around a completely empty canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象一个漆成金色的画框，里面却是一张空白画布。

examples.en: The trial was dismissed as a legal farce.
examples.cn: 那场审判被视为一场法律闹剧而不予理会。

examples.en: The play is a farce about two clerks who lose a coffin.
examples.cn: 这出戏是一出闹剧，讲两个职员弄丢了一口棺材。

examples.en: The ceremony collapsed into farce when the wrong anthem played.
examples.cn: 放错国歌时，典礼沦为一场闹剧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发斯」——像台上的人被塞得鼓鼓囊囊，一开口就发出笑声；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 farcire（填塞）→ farcimen（馅料）→ 法语 farce（馅料；插进戏剧的滑稽段）→ 英语 farce，核心义「被塞进去的笑料，进而指荒唐场面」。

sensesIntro.en: Farce starts as a stuffed comic play, then names the absurdity of real events, the hollow show that pretends to be serious, and finally the old kitchen stuffing.
sensesIntro.cn: farce 先指塞满笑料的滑稽戏，再指现实事件的荒唐、徒有其表的严肃表演，最后保留古老的烹饪「馅料」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage prop stuffed so full that the lid will not shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件道具被塞得太满，盖子都合不上。

branches.en: The stage comedy is the founding sense.
branches.cn: 舞台喜剧是本义。

branches.en: The absurd real event is the transferred branch.
branches.cn: 荒唐的现实事件是转移后的分支。

branches.en: The hollow pretence is the moral branch.
branches.cn: 徒有其表的假象是道德层面的分支。

branches.en: The cooking stuffing is the oldest literal branch.
branches.cn: 烹饪里的馅料是最古老的字面分支。

branches.en: The kitchen sense and the stage sense share the same stuffing image.
branches.cn: 厨房义与舞台义共享同一个「填塞」意象。

intro.en: Farce is a Latin verb turned noun: farcire, to stuff, gives farcimen, stuffing, and French farce, the comic material stuffed into a play.
intro.cn: farce 是拉丁语动词变来的名词：farcire（填塞）给出 farcimen（馅料）与法语 farce（塞进戏里的滑稽材料）。

latinIntro.en: Latin farcire means to stuff; farcimen means stuffing, and the family keeps the kitchen image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 farcire 意为填塞；farcimen 意为馅料，整个词族保留着厨房的意象。

items.example: Farcire is the literal source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: farcire 是整个词族的字面来源。

items.example: Farcimen keeps the kitchen sense alive.
items.exampleCN: farcimen 让厨房义得以保存。

items.example: Fartus is the participle behind the stuffing image.
items.exampleCN: fartus 是「填塞」意象背后的分词形式。

items.example: French farce adds the theatrical twist.
items.exampleCN: 法语 farce 加上了戏剧性的转折。

items.meaning: a comic play; an absurd event
items.example: English farce widens from the stage to real life.
items.exampleCN: 英语 farce 从舞台扩展到现实生活。

items.example: Farcical describes events that play like comedy.
items.exampleCN: farcical 形容像喜剧一样上演的事件。

items.example: Farcically marks the comic manner of an action.
items.exampleCN: farcically 标记一个动作的滑稽方式。

items.meaning: a writer or performer of farces
items.example: Farceur names the person who makes the farce.
items.exampleCN: farceur 指创作或演出闹剧的人。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事之人的后缀

definition_zh: 票价；费
definition_en: the money paid for a journey, or to get on in a particular way
core_image: 公交车门口，乘客刷卡付费后走向座位
scene: 他刷卡付了公交车费。He paid the bus fare with a card.
sceneCN: 这里 fare 是「车费」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他刷卡支付了公交车费。

senses.title: Travel price
senses.definition: the money a passenger pays for a journey
senses.definitionCN: 乘客为一段行程支付的钱
senses.example: The train fare has gone up again.
senses.exampleCN: 火车票价又涨了。
senses.why: The core sense is the price of being carried.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是被运送所需支付的价格。

senses.title: Cost of food or service
senses.definition: the cost of meals, entertainment, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 餐食、娱乐或服务的费用
senses.example: The hotel offers simple local fare.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店提供简单的当地饭菜。
senses.why: Travel costs extend to the cost of food along the way.
senses.whyCN: 旅途开销扩展为途中饮食的费用。

senses.title: Get on in life
senses.definition: to experience good or bad fortune in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某情境中经历好运或坏运
senses.example: The team fared well in the competition.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在比赛中表现出色。
senses.why: How a journey goes becomes how life goes.
senses.whyCN: 旅程如何变成生活如何。

intro.en: Fare comes from Old English faran, to journey, and faru, a journey.
intro.cn: fare 源自古英语 faran（旅行）与 faru（旅程）。

items.en: Faran meant to travel.
items.cn: faran 意为旅行。

items.en: Faran meant to go or journey; faru meant a journey.
items.cn: faran 意为行走、旅行；faru 意为旅程。

items.en: Fare named the cost of a journey.
items.cn: fare 指旅程的费用。

items.en: Fare extended to food provided for a journey.
items.cn: fare 扩展到旅途中提供的食物。

items.en: Fare means a ticket price or how someone gets on.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fare 指票价或某人的境遇。

note.en: Fare is compared with homophones and with words for prices.
note.cn: 把 fare 与同音词以及表示价格的词作比较。

entries.definition: the money needed to buy something
the money asked for a service

normalIntro.en: Fare and fair sound the same but one is money and one is justice.
normalIntro.cn: fare 与 fair 同音，但一个指钱，一个指公平。

normal.en: Fare is what you pay to travel.
normal.cn: fare 是你出行要付的钱。

normal.en: Fair is justice; fare is money, so keep the e.
normal.cn: fair 是公平，fare 是钱，注意 fare 有 e。

normal.en: Fare well means get on well.
normal.cn: fare well 意为进展顺利。

normal.en: Bus fare and train fare are everyday phrases.
normal.cn: bus fare 和 train fare 是日常搭配。

normal.en: Fare as food appears in local fare and simple fare.
normal.cn: fare 指食物时见于 local fare 与 simple fare。

abstract.en: A fare is the price of moving from one place to another.
abstract.cn: 票价是从一处到另一处的代价。

abstract.en: How you fare is how your journey through events goes.
abstract.cn: 你 fare 得如何，就是你在事件旅程中走得如何。

abstract.en: One word covers travel cost, food, and fortune.
abstract.cn: 一个词涵盖旅费、食物与命运。

examples.en: How much is the fare to the airport?
examples.cn: 到机场的票价是多少？

examples.en: The children pay half fare.
examples.cn: 孩子们付半价。

examples.en: The small restaurant serves simple fare.
examples.cn: 这家小餐馆供应简单的饭菜。

dict_mnemonic.text: fare 与 fair 同音；fair 是「公平」，fare 是「出行要付的钱」，也可指旅途中的饭菜与境遇。

root: 源自古英语 faran（旅行）与 faru（旅程），核心义「一段旅程所需的代价与经历」。

sensesIntro.en: Fare means the price of a journey, the cost of food or service, or how someone gets on.
sensesIntro.cn: fare 意为旅费、餐食或服务费用，或某人的境遇进展。

core.en: The cost and experience of a journey.
core.cn: 一段旅程的代价与经历。

branches.en: The price paid for transport.
branches.cn: 为交通支付的价钱。

branches.en: The cost of meals and service.
branches.cn: 餐食与服务费用。

branches.en: How a person or team gets on.
branches.cn: 人或团队的进展境遇。

branches.en: Travel and food both cost money.
branches.cn: 出行与饮食都要花钱。

branches.en: A journey and a life both have a fare.
branches.cn: 旅程与人生都有其「代价与走向」。

intro.en: Fare forms compounds about tickets and travel.
intro.cn: fare 构成关于票务与旅行的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Fare is Germanic, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: fare 属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.meaning: a travel price or to get on

items.example: They fared badly in the storm.
items.exampleCN: 他们在风暴中境况不佳。

items.meaning: a card used to pay fares
a person who travels on foot

definition_zh: 告别；辞别
definition_en: an act of saying goodbye, or a parting wish of good fortune
core_image: 月台上，两个朋友拥抱后挥手，列车缓缓启动
scene: 毕业那天，学生们向老师挥手告别。The students waved farewell to their teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 farewell 是「告别」（第 1 个义项）；句意：学生们向老师挥手告别。

senses.title: Act of parting
senses.definition: the act of saying goodbye to someone who is leaving
senses.definitionCN: 向即将离开的人道别的行为
senses.example: They said their farewells at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站道别。
senses.why: The core sense is the moment of parting.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是分别的时刻。

senses.title: Parting event
senses.definition: a party or ceremony held for someone who is leaving
senses.definitionCN: 为即将离开的人举行的聚会或仪式
senses.example: The office held a farewell for her.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室为她举办了告别会。
senses.why: The goodbye becomes an organized occasion.
senses.whyCN: 道别变成有组织的场合。

senses.title: Parting greeting
senses.definition: a word said when leaving, wishing someone well
senses.definitionCN: 离开时说的话，祝愿对方安好
senses.example: Farewell, and good luck!
senses.exampleCN: 再见，祝你好运！
senses.why: The wish for good travel becomes a single greeting.
senses.whyCN: 对旅途顺利的祝愿变成一个问候语。

intro.en: Farewell joins fare, to journey, and well, a wish for good fortune.
intro.cn: farewell 由 fare（旅行）与 well（安好）组合而成，意为祝愿旅途顺利。

items.en: Faran meant to journey; wel meant well.
items.cn: faran 意为旅行；wel 意为好。

items.en: Fare wel was said as a parting wish.
items.cn: fare wel 作为分别祝愿使用。

items.en: Farewell became one word for a goodbye.
items.cn: farewell 合为一个词表示告别。

items.en: Farewell parties and speeches became common.
items.cn: 告别会和告别演说变得常见。

items.en: Farewell is formal and slightly literary.
items.cn: 现代英语中 farewell 较正式且略带文学色彩。

note.en: Farewell is compared with similar forms and with other parting words.
note.cn: 把 farewell 与形近形式以及其他告别用语作比较。

normalIntro.en: Farewell literally means travel well, a wish for the road ahead.
normalIntro.cn: farewell 字面意为「一路安好」，是对前路的祝愿。

normal.en: Farewell is fare plus well, travel well.
normal.cn: farewell 是 fare 加 well，意为旅途安好。

normal.en: Bid farewell is a formal way to say goodbye.
normal.cn: bid farewell 是正式的道别说法。

normal.en: A farewell party marks a departure.
normal.cn: 告别会标志一次离开。

normal.en: Farewell is stronger and more formal than bye.
normal.cn: farewell 比 bye 更强烈也更正式。

normal.en: The plural farewells means several goodbyes.
normal.cn: 复数 farewells 意为多次道别。

abstract.en: Every farewell holds a wish for the journey ahead.
abstract.cn: 每一次告别都包含对前路的祝愿。

abstract.en: Saying farewell makes an ending visible.
abstract.cn: 告别让一个结束变得可见。

abstract.en: The word is a small gift of good fortune.
abstract.cn: 这个词是祝愿对方好运的小礼物。

examples.en: We bade her farewell at the airport.
examples.cn: 我们在机场向她道别。

examples.en: The team held a farewell dinner for the coach.
examples.cn: 球队为教练举办了告别晚宴。

examples.en: He waved farewell from the train window.
examples.cn: 他从火车窗口挥手告别。

dict_mnemonic.text: fare 是「旅行」，well 是「安好」，farewell 即「祝你旅途安好」，用作告别语。

root: 由 fare（旅行）与 well（安好）组成的中古英语告别语，核心义「祝前路顺利的分别」。

sensesIntro.en: Farewell means the act of parting, a parting event, or a formal word of goodbye.
sensesIntro.cn: farewell 意为告别行为、告别活动，或正式的再见用语。

core.en: A parting wish for the other's journey.
core.cn: 对他人旅途的分别祝愿。

branches.en: The act of saying goodbye.
branches.cn: 说道别的行为。

branches.en: A gathering held for a departing person.
branches.cn: 为离开者举行的聚会。

branches.en: The spoken word of parting.
branches.cn: 说出口的告别语。

branches.en: The act and the word happen together.
branches.cn: 告别行为与告别语同时发生。

branches.en: A private goodbye can become a public event.
branches.cn: 私人的道别可以成为公开活动。

intro.en: Farewell is a compound of two native English words.
intro.cn: farewell 是两个英语本族词构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Farewell is Germanic, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: farewell 属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to journey or a travel price

items.example: He gave a short farewell speech.
items.exampleCN: 他作了简短的告别演说。

items.example: The soup was done to a fare-thee-well.

definition_zh: 农场；农田；耕种；务农
definition_en: an area of land used for growing crops or keeping animals, or to work such land
core_image: 清晨的农场，拖拉机驶过整齐的田垄，牛羊在远处吃草
scene: 天刚亮，他就开着拖拉机去农场干活。At dawn he drove his tractor to the farm to work.
sceneCN: 这里 farm 是「农场」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天刚亮，他就开着拖拉机去农场干活。

senses.title: Land for crops and animals
senses.definition: an area of land and buildings used for growing crops or keeping animals
senses.definitionCN: 用于种植作物或饲养牲畜的一片土地及建筑
senses.example: They keep cows and sheep on the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在农场里养奶牛和绵羊。
senses.why: The basic modern sense is a working piece of agricultural land.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义就是一块用于农业生产的土地。

senses.title: A specialized production site
senses.definition: a place where a particular animal or crop is produced on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 大规模生产某种动物或作物的场地
senses.example: The fish farm supplies the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这家渔场供应整个地区。
senses.why: Specialized production narrows the land sense to one product.
senses.whyCN: 专业化生产把土地义缩小到单一产品。

senses.title: To work the land
senses.definition: to grow crops or keep animals as a business
senses.definitionCN: 以种植作物或饲养牲畜为业
senses.example: Her family has farmed this valley for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 她的家族在这个山谷里耕种了好几代。
senses.why: The verb turns the place into a continuing activity.
senses.whyCN: 动词义把场所变成持续进行的活动。

intro.en: Farm comes from Old English feorm, meaning food, supplies, or a rent paid in goods.
intro.cn: farm 源自古英语 feorm，意为食物、供给或用实物支付的地租。

items.en: Feorm meant food, supplies, or a rent paid in goods.
items.cn: feorm 意为食物、供给或用实物支付的地租。

items.en: Ferme came to mean land held for a fixed rent.
items.cn: ferme 开始表示按固定地租持有的土地。

items.en: The meaning shifted to land used for agriculture.
items.cn: 词义转向用于农业的土地。

items.en: Farm covered both the land and the business of working it.
items.cn: farm 同时指土地和经营土地的事业。

items.en: Farm is now the everyday word for agricultural land.
items.cn: 现代英语中 farm 是表示农业土地的日常用词。

note.en: Farm is compared with similar short words and with words for large agricultural places.
note.cn: 把 farm 与形近的短词以及表示大型农业场地的词作比较。

entries.definition: a shape, or a printed paper
the state of being well known
a large farm for cattle or horses
a large estate growing one crop

normalIntro.en: Farm is the place, farmer is the person, and farming is the work.
normalIntro.cn: farm 是场所，farmer 是人，farming 是工作。

normal.en: Farm hides the short word far plus an m.
normal.cn: farm 可以看成 far 后面加一个 m。

normal.en: A farmer works on a farm.
normal.cn: farmer 在 farm 上干活。

normal.en: A dairy farm produces milk.
normal.cn: 奶牛场生产牛奶。

normal.en: Farmland is the land of a farm.
normal.cn: farmland 就是农场的土地。

normal.en: The f at the start can stand for food.
normal.cn: 开头的 f 可以联想为 food（食物）。

abstract.en: The core of farm is not crops but support: land that feeds people.
abstract.cn: farm 的核心不是作物，而是供养：土地供养人。

abstract.en: From rent to cultivation, farm always concerns the use of land.
abstract.cn: 从地租到耕种，farm 始终围绕土地的使用权。

abstract.en: A farm is both a physical place and an economic unit.
abstract.cn: 农场既是地理空间，也是经济单位。

examples.en: The farm grows wheat and corn.
examples.cn: 这个农场种小麦和玉米。

examples.en: They run a small dairy farm.
examples.cn: 他们经营一个小型奶牛场。

examples.en: My grandfather farmed this land for forty years.
examples.cn: 我祖父在这片土地上耕种了四十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: farm 源自古英语 feorm（食物、地租），从「以食物交租的土地」演变为「农场」；加上表人的后缀就是 farmer。

root: 源自古英语 feorm（食物、供给、地租），核心义「供养人的土地与出产」。

sensesIntro.en: Farm means land for crops and animals, a specialized production site, or the work of cultivating land.
sensesIntro.cn: farm 意为种植养殖的土地、专业化生产场地，或耕种土地的行为。

core.en: A piece of land that feeds people.
core.cn: 一块供养人们的土地。

branches.en: Land that grows crops and keeps animals.
branches.cn: 种植作物、饲养牲畜的土地。

branches.en: A site devoted to one product, such as fish.
branches.cn: 专门生产一种产品的场地，如渔场。

branches.en: The activity of working such land.
branches.cn: 经营这类土地的活动。

branches.en: Both senses name a place of agricultural production.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指农业生产场所。

branches.en: The place and the work share the same word.
branches.cn: 场所与劳作共用同一个词。

intro.en: Farm builds a large English family for land, people, and buildings.
intro.cn: farm 构成一个包含土地、人物与建筑的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Old English feorm is the source; farm has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 feorm 是词源，farm 没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: land for crops, or to work land

items.exampleCN: 这些田地采用有机方式耕种。

items.meaning: a person who runs a farm
the main house on a farm
items.exampleCN: 他们修复了一座老农舍。

definition_zh: 使着迷；强烈吸引；蛊惑
definition_en: to interest or attract someone very strongly, or to bewitch by magic in older use
core_image: 孩子趴在玻璃前，目不转睛地看一条盘绕的蛇
scene: 恐龙化石让全班同学着迷。Dinosaur fossils fascinate the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里 fascinate 是「使着迷」（第 1 个义项）；句意：恐龙化石让全班同学着迷。

senses.title: To attract strongly
senses.definition: to interest or attract someone very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地引起某人的兴趣或吸引某人
senses.example: The old photographs fascinate her.
senses.exampleCN: 那些老照片让她着迷。
senses.why: The main modern sense is intense, lasting interest.
senses.whyCN: 主要现代义是强烈而持久的兴趣。

senses.title: To hold the gaze
senses.definition: to hold someone's attention so that they cannot look away
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住某人的注意力，使其无法移开视线
senses.example: The dancer's movement fascinated the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者的动作让观众看得目不转睛。
senses.why: The sense stresses attention fixed on one sight.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项强调注意力被固定在一个画面上。

senses.title: To bewitch
senses.definition: to put someone under a magic spell, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 在较古老或文学用法中，用魔法迷住某人
senses.example: In the tale, a spirit fascinates the traveler.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，一个精灵用魔法迷住了旅人。
senses.why: The original sense was literal magic.
senses.whyCN: 最初的义项就是字面意义上的魔法。

intro.en: Fascinate comes from Latin fascinare, to bewitch, and first meant to enchant by magic.
intro.cn: fascinate 源自拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法），最初意为用魔法迷住。

items.en: Fascinare meant to bewitch or put under a spell.
items.cn: fascinare 意为施魔法或使人中咒。

items.en: Fascinum was a spell or a charm against evil.
items.cn: fascinum 指咒语或辟邪的护符。

items.en: English fascinate meant to enchant by magic.
items.cn: 英语 fascinate 意为用魔法迷住。

items.en: The sense widened to mean charm or captivate.
items.cn: 词义扩大为使人倾心或着迷。

items.en: Fascinate now means to interest someone intensely.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fascinate 意为强烈地引起兴趣。

note.en: Fascinate is compared with related forms and with verbs for holding attention.
note.cn: 把 fascinate 与相关词形以及表示抓住注意力的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fascinate is the verb behind fascinating and fascination.
normalIntro.cn: fascinate 是 fascinating 与 fascination 背后的动词。

normal.en: Fascinate hides the sound of fascinating.
normal.cn: fascinate 与 fascinating 的发音相近。

normal.en: Be fascinated by means to be strongly attracted.
normal.cn: be fascinated by 意为被强烈吸引。

normal.en: A fascinating story holds the reader.
normal.cn: fascinating 的故事能抓住读者。

normal.en: Fascinate is stronger than interest.
normal.cn: fascinate 的语气比 interest 更强。

normal.en: Fascination is the feeling and the power to attract.
normal.cn: fascination 既指着迷的感觉，也指吸引力。

abstract.en: The force of fascinate lies in the idea of not being able to look away.
abstract.cn: fascinate 的力量来自「无法移开」这一动作。

abstract.en: From magic to charm, attention is held by something outside the self.
abstract.cn: 从魔法到魅力，注意力都被自身之外的东西掌控。

abstract.en: What fascinates us both attracts us and takes away our control.
abstract.cn: 让人着迷的事物既吸引人，也让人失去自主。

examples.en: Snakes fascinate many children.
examples.cn: 蛇让许多孩子着迷。

examples.en: She was fascinated by the old maps.
examples.cn: 她被那些旧地图深深吸引。

examples.en: The speaker fascinated the audience for an hour.
examples.cn: 演讲者让听众着迷了一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: fascinate 源自拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法），原义是「用魔法定住」，后来引申为「使人着迷」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法、蛊惑），核心义「用魔力定住目光与心神」。

sensesIntro.en: Fascinate means to attract someone strongly, to hold the gaze, or in older use to bewitch.
sensesIntro.cn: fascinate 意为强烈吸引某人、使目光无法移开，或在旧用法中施魔法蛊惑。

core.en: An attraction that holds attention and will not let go.
core.cn: 一种让人无法移开注意力的吸引力。

branches.en: Strong interest in something.
branches.cn: 对某物产生强烈兴趣。

branches.en: Attention fixed on a single sight.
branches.cn: 注意力固定在一个画面上。

branches.en: Magic that holds a person.
branches.cn: 用魔法控制一个人。

branches.en: Both describe attention one cannot break.
branches.cn: 两者都描述无法打断的注意力。

branches.en: Both suggest a force beyond ordinary will.
branches.cn: 两者都暗示超出意志的力量。

intro.en: Fascinate grows into nouns, adjectives, and adverbs about intense attraction.
intro.cn: fascinate 衍生出表示强烈吸引的名词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fascinare, to bewitch, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法）是直接词源。

items.example: We were fascinated by the film.
items.exampleCN: 我们被这部电影迷住了。
她讲了一个引人入胜的故事。
这本书细节丰富得令人着迷。

items.meaning: a state or power of strong attraction
items.example: His fascination with birds began young.
items.exampleCN: 他对鸟类的着迷始于幼年。

items.meaning: a decorative head covering, or a person who charms

items.example: His fascinations range from stars to shells.
items.exampleCN: 他着迷的东西从星星到贝壳都有。
